Phainon wakes up with his heart already pounding and a vague sense of dread settling low in his stomach. It’s the kind that sinks in before he’s even fully conscious, as though his body remembers something awful before his brain has the chance to catch up. He sighs, long and quiet, blinking through the crust on his eyelashes and the sleep still clinging annoyingly to the corners of his eyes.

His limbs feel heavy, stuck somewhere between exhaustion and restlessness. Phainon rubs at his face, wiping away the blur until the ceiling above him comes into sharp focus - plain, familiar, and yet somehow as unsettling as his racing thoughts. The early morning stillness of his room doesn’t soothe him. If anything, it makes everything worse. There’s no distraction here, nothing to pull his mind away from how his chest tightens at the memory of Mydei’s flushed cheeks, parted lips, the way his voice had gone so quiet when he said: “You did well.”

Phainon exhales again, this time shakily, and presses his palms to his face, willing the weight of it all to suddenly lift and disappear as quickly as Mydei did last night back into his room. He can’t lie - it stung. It still does, right around his heart, creating this roiling, hot feeling that he can’t get rid of. It’s like he has heartburn, but no amount of rubbing at his chest or drinking water can shift it. He knows more than anyone that he fucked up last night. He pushed too far, too soon and far too quickly, acting out on a deep-seated whim at trying to consume as much as he could.

But, as much as he hates it, the guilt wrapped around the whole situation is laced with something sweet. It’s the knowledge that he did that to Mydei. His hands, his mouth, and his presence made Mydei react like that: made him flustered, breathless, hard, undone in a way Phainon had never seen before and couldn’t stop replaying in his head on a loop. It sparks in his chest like a struck match, and even though he knows he shouldn’t enjoy it - Mydei had clearly been uncomfortable, going by his abrupt exit - he absolutely, horribly, does.

Phainon kicks his legs under the duvet, thrashing like it’ll shake off the feeling, but it only makes his grin stretch wider. His frown is nothing more than forgotten, crumpling under the force of giddiness bubbling up in him. He tries to smother it, biting down on his lip and the inside of his cheek, but it’s too late. His whole body feels warm, jittery, and alive. The situation has well and truly settled in; he’s allowed to kiss Mydei. He’s been kissing Mydei, with varying degrees of success, but last night he’d been given a compliment in two ways: verbal and physical.

“Okay, okay, calm down,” Phainon mutters to himself through his smile, rolling onto his side and burying his face into his pillow. Elation pours through him like a wave - bright and uninvited, and far too much for six in the morning. It’s the kind of happiness that feels a little wrong, like laughing when you’re not supposed to. It’s a twisted, breathless sort of joy that leaves him feeling slightly ill with himself as he clings to it.

He wriggles around until he’s on his front, hands shoved under his pillows as he kicks up his duvet, revelling in the cool air that ghosts around his overheated legs. Mydei had looked stunning last night, all glassy eyes and bruised lips, his inner thighs scorching hot from the heat coming from his - ah, Phainon can’t even finish the thought. He squirms in his bed, hips moving side to side, the friction doing its job against his own half-hard cock to take the edge off. Even just picturing and remembering how good it felt to kiss Mydei’s jaw, and then kiss him properly is enough to make desire throb in his veins.

Phainon can’t help but wonder what would’ve happened if Mydei had let him touch a little further - just a little more. The thought creeps in uninvited, slow and heavy, winding around his ribs and deep in his gut. He remembers clearly the smooth warmth of Mydei’s skin beneath his palm, how natural it felt to touch him there, how electric. The way his thigh had tensed, muscles quivering like Mydei wasn’t entirely unaffected like he was holding something back. Phainon’s fingers had flirted just beneath the hem of those ridiculous little shorts that Mydei insists on wearing to bed - barely even shorts at all, really, more suggestion than fabric. If he’d been allowed to move higher, to drag his fingertips just another inch, to map out the rest of his skin and feel what Mydei had so desperately been running away from, what then? What kind of reaction would he have gotten from that - something different to their kisses? Something more, something less? More intense, or dialled down?

“Alright, that’s enough,” Phainon says once again to himself, hauling himself up onto his knees. He glances down at the tent in his shorts, sighing as he yanks the length of his shirt over it. There’s technically nothing stopping him from jacking off again thinking of Mydei, but then he’d have to deal with even more shame than he’s already packing.

With that, he drags himself out of bed a full ten minutes after deciding to. He almost trips over his duvet still wrapped around his legs, having to catch himself by doing some hops until he’s steady again. Phainon is well and truly awake, and the panic of almost falling has settled the problem area between his legs for now. He runs a hand through his hair in lieu of doing anything useful to it, wandering over to his desk to peer at himself in the small mirror he keeps on there.

He doesn’t look terrible, but he doesn’t look great, either. His sleep had been plagued with thoughts of Mydei and half-twisted nightmares of things he’d rather not remember. It’s always been like that when it comes to sleep - Mydei, strong and beautiful until he’s not, mixed in with the terror and morphing into something else he can’t recognise along with his parents and sister that pop up during the night.

Phainon clears his throat, the sound too loud in the quiet flat, and gives his head a sharp shake as if that’ll dislodge the thoughts clinging stubbornly to his brain. There’s no point dwelling on fantasies and what-ifs - not when he’s got more pressing things to stress over. Like the far less hypothetical, very real question of how he’s supposed to look Mydei in the eye this morning without spontaneously combusting.

He cringes at the thought, lips tugging downward in automatic distaste. It’s one thing to roll around in bed like some lovesick fool, grinning into his pillow and reliving every second of that kiss - but it’s a completely different thing when he remembers he has no idea what Mydei’s perspective is of last night. He has nothing, nada, not a single gauge, hint or suggestion apart from the anxious tension lining his body as he walked away. Mydei had pulled away before anything substantial could be discussed about what just happened, leaving Phainon alone with nothing but his own thoughts.

Phainon’s known Mydei for two years - lived with him for nearly one - and still, right now, he feels like a stranger trying to read a language he’s never studied. But that’s not true because ever since they met, Phainon’s done nothing but study Mydei. That’s what rattles him the most as Mydei has always been familiar. Predictable, even. And now? Now Phainon doesn’t know where he stands - where their friendship stands - or if he’s even standing at all in the same play park as Mydei at all.

He slaps his cheeks, allowing the sting of skin hitting skin to wake him up even more and snap him out of this downward spiral. Phainon walks to his bedroom door, opening it to the sounds of Mydei puttering around in the kitchen, just like always. It eases something in his heart, his fingers relaxing on the door handle as he lets go and makes his way over.

The hallway feels longer than usual. Every step of bare feet against the wooden floor echoes just a little too loudly. He rounds the corner into the kitchen like someone expecting to be ambushed - and maybe, emotionally, he is. Mydei’s already there, standing at the counter with his back to Phainon, leaning slightly as the kettle rumbles quietly towards a boil. His posture is easy, unguarded in the way he gets when he doesn’t realise he’s being watched: shoulders relaxed, head tilted ever so slightly to one side like he’s still waking up.

He’s wearing one of Phainon’s hoodies - a pastel pink one that’s seen better days, its cuffs fraying and seams soft from years of wear and too many washes. It hangs loose even on Mydei’s big frame, sleeves bunched at the wrists, the fabric swallowing him whole in a way that makes something ache in Phainon’s chest. His hair is all down this morning, not even hastily tied back like he does sometimes in the mornings to get it out of his face. It falls in soft waves across his shoulders, a few strands flicking into the hood, some caught and tucked in awkwardly like they’ve been there all night.

Phainon notices with a small smile that the hood is inside out. Of course it is. Without thinking, he crosses the room. There’s a quiet fondness blooming in his chest - gentle, familiar, warm. He huffs a soft laugh, mostly to himself, and reaches out to move Mydei’s hair with careful fingers, brushing it aside so it doesn’t get caught as he begins turning the hood right-side in.

Mydei jumps slightly, startled by the sudden touch, and Phainon feels the jolt of it in his own skin. He doesn’t move away, though, not yet. He’s got a job to do. His hands linger on the ends of Mydei’s hair for a second longer than necessary. Mydei glances over his shoulder, eyes wide in surprise, cheeks slightly flushed as their gazes meet. Phainon grounds himself in the simplicity of the gesture - offering Mydei a grin as he finishes pushing the hood inside with a flourish - and almost drowning with the weight of wanting someone he can’t have as Mydei smiles back at him.

“I made you tea,” Mydei says, his voice slightly scratchy from disuse after sleeping.

“Thanks,” Phainon replies, eye twitching minutely at how hot Mydei sounds so early in the morning. It’s another thing that he’s had to get used to after living with him - but it still doesn’t make it any easier.

“Do you want me to grab the milk?” Phainon asks, peering over Mydei’s shoulder to watch him pour the hot water into their mugs. “Wait, how did you know I was awake to even want tea?”

Mydei shoulders him out of the way and gets the milk from the fridge, setting it down next to Phainon to pour himself. “I could hear you being stupid in your room.”

“What!” Phainon exclaims, almost overflowing his mug with milk until Mydei snatches it away from him. “I wasn’t - that -”

“You were giggling to yourself,” Mydei clarifies as if Phainon needed to hear confirmation that Mydei had heard him being an idiot earlier.

“Shut up,” Phainon says without any heat behind it, trying to will the blood in his cheeks to cool off.

They stand in silence as Phainon watches Mydei top his mug off with milk before grabbing their pot of sugar, piling in at least 5 teaspoons worth into the drink.

“Gross,” Phainon comments, face scrunching up.

“You’re gross,” Mydei shoots back, gesturing to Phainon’s mug. “Your tea is almost as white as you are.”

“Hey!” Phainon is really pouting now, cradling his mug in his hands almost protectively. “Just because I can’t tan during the summer…”

“You turn into a big red lobster instead,” Mydei replies, putting the milk away and wiping down the counter free of sugar granules. “It’s cute.” He finishes, far too offhandedly.

“Stop,” Phainon groans, dragging the word out dramatically. He wants to hide behind his hands but instead, he hides behind his mug, taking a pre-emptive sip knowing it hasn’t cooled down properly yet. He winces and holds in a curse. Deserved.

For a moment, it’s quiet again - just the faint clink of the spoon against the side of Mydei’s cup as he stirs, slower than necessary. Phainon’s eyebrows furrow as he feels the silence thicken, his shoulders rising to his ears as he takes another gulp of his tea to help settle the funny feeling in his stomach at the sudden change in atmosphere. He thought they were okay - the relaxed feeling he gets while being around Mydei hadn’t gotten up and disappeared, instead it’d simply proven itself by sticking around as soon as he laid eyes on Mydei in their kitchen.

Then, Mydei speaks: “Can you sit down for a sec?” He asks, not looking up as he sets the spoon aside. “There’s something we need to discuss.”

Immediately, Phainon feels uneasy. He feels sick, hot and then cold, sweaty and clammy, faint and dizzy all at once. That’s never a good thing to hear, is it? If they were dating - which to Phainon’s dismay, they’re not - this would definitely lead up to a breakup. When does hearing anything along those lines of ‘we need to talk’ lead to anything good?

“Uh, yeah, sure,” Phainon stutters, going to put his mug down but then deciding against it, bringing it with him as Mydei leads them over to their dining table.

As Phainon sits down, he notices that Mydei’s notebook and pencil case are already laid out on the table, spread across the surface like he’s been studying since some godforsaken hour of the morning. Everything is neat - too neat. The notebook sits squarely in the centre, pages already turned to a blank spread, pencil resting perfectly parallel to the spine. His pencil case has been unzipped and rifled through, pens organised by colour like Mydei had been fidgeting for something to do with his hands.

Phainon watches him for a moment, full of trepidation. Mydei doesn’t meet his eyes. He’s standing stiffly by the other chair, shifting his weight from foot to foot like he’s working up the courage to deliver bad news. Phainon opens his mouth to speak but then closes it again, his teeth clacking together as Mydei finally moves, joltingly pulling the chair out and sitting down far too carefully, like he’s hyper-aware of every movement. Everything about this puts Phainon more and more on edge. Mydei is many things - blunt, strong, and sharp-tongued when he wants to be - but nervous isn’t usually one of them. Phainon can’t even recall Mydei acting nervy before big rugby matches against other universities, instead basking in the excitement of a potentially good match. He’s never been like this - and certainly not around Phainon.

The quiet clink of Mydei’s mug meeting the table startles Phainon out of his thoughts. He flinches slightly, eyes snapping to where Mydei is already moving - gathering up his notebook and pen with a kind of focused urgency, flipping past one page, then another, until he lands on whatever it is he’s been meaning to show.

Phainon swallows hard. His heart is thundering in his chest, an erratic rhythm that’s all wrong - too fast, too heavy. It echoes in his ears, pounding so violently that for one terrifying moment, he’s convinced it might either stop entirely or crack straight out of his ribcage and splatter itself across the table. He grips the edge of the chair to ground himself, knuckles white, trying to prepare for whatever is about to come. But Mydei says nothing yet, his focus finally locking onto a single page. He clears his throat, sitting up straighter in his chair. Phainon’s dread tenfolds as Mydei opens his mouth.

“I have a list -”

Phainon’s mouth drops open, a rush of emotions overflowing so much he can’t tell them apart. “Ah! Why is it okay for you to make a list, but it’s embarrassing when I do?! Not fair!”

Mydei levels him with a venomous glare, “Shut up and listen.”

Phainon holds his hands up in surrender.

“I have a list -” Mydei ignores Phainon’s scoff. “Of boundaries.”

“Oh,” Phainon says simply, guilt creeping back up on him. He supposes it makes sense after he definitely crossed the boundaries of what was okay last night.

“Are you going to listen or do I need to bribe you with a treat?” Mydei asks.

“I’m not actually a dog, y’know,” Phainon sniffs haughtily, “But… if you could make protein waffles for breakfast, I’ll do the dishes?” He throws in his best pleading look after to hopefully sweeten the pot.

“You’d do the dishes anyway,” Mydei says, flicking at his nose. Phainon pouts and rubs the sore spot. “Fine. I’ll make waffles after this.”

Phainon fist pumps the air, much to Mydei’s dismay, and quickly settles down again, realising that this conversation they’re about to have is important. The weight of it dawns on him quickly, replacing his brief triumph with a flicker of nerves. He clenches his hands into fists on the tops of his thighs to give them something to do, nervously shifting in his seat to try and get comfortable again. Phainon doesn’t even know where to look or how serious his face should be, and no matter how much he tries to make his expression fall neutral, he can’t help the pinch in his brow and the subtle downwards turn of his lips.

“Okay, so, rule number one,” Mydei begins, voice clear and slightly raised in volume. It makes Phainon sit up even straighter, shoulders pushed back as though he’s about to be called upon during a lecture. “Keep any kissing in private. That means nothing happens outside of this flat, got it?”

Phainon salutes, “Got it.”

Mydei nods once, going back to looking at his notepad. “Rule number two. If you want to stop, you have to tell me immediately.”

Phainon’s head jerks back slightly, the thought of not wanting to kiss Mydei seems impossible. Ridiculous. Preposterous, even. “Same goes for you, too,” He tags on.

Mydei blinks at him, “If I want to stop kissing?”

“Yes…?” Phainon says slowly, gesturing to the list. “If I can say no, so can you. We need to be on the same wavelength at all times when doing this. Plus, you’re the teacher, so if you don’t wanna teach anymore, you gotta say something.”

Mydei mutters something under his breath that sounds suspiciously like the word unlikely, but he shakes his head and his eyes are back on the notebook before Phainon can question it.

“Rule number three…” Mydei trails off, his voice quieter now, eyes glued to the page as though he can’t bring himself to look up. A flush blossoms across his face, starting at the tip of his nose before spreading outwards until his cheeks, ears, and even the slope of his neck are tinged with red. He presses his lips together, clearly debating whether to say it at all.

Phainon watches it all, spellbound and unbearably warm. There’s something about seeing Mydei flustered like this that makes his stomach twist in ways that he’s not prepared to deal with. It makes him want to reach over and feel the heat beneath his palms, under his lips and below his tongue as he tastes the flushed skin for himself.

“No hands under clothes,” Mydei finally finishes, sounding firmer than before, although the embarrassment of the statement clearly still clings to every syllable.

Phainon feels like the floor should open up and swallow him whole. His entire body tenses, like if he holds still enough, he might actually manage to disappear into the grout between the tiles under him. His face burns hotter than the tea he nearly scalded himself on earlier, and he’s not sure if the heat in his chest is shame or something far more dangerous. Probably both. It’s obvious they’re both remembering last night. How could they not? It’s undoubtedly fresh, the feeling of Mydei’s hardness at his fingertips makes them tingle, his entire hands turning to static as he wishes he could’ve had more.

“Sure, easy, I can do that,” Phainon replies because he is stupid but wants to respect whatever Mydei is saying to him. If it’s a boundary - one he’s guessing sparked this entire list to begin with - then it’s a serious one that he won’t cross.

Should he apologise for last night? That’d be the correct thing to do, right? It’d at least soothe something in his soul if nothing else, but deep down, past all the guilt and shame and other tangles of feelings he doesn’t want to go into, he doesn’t regret it. If anything, he’s been thriving off the small touch he got; the peek of Mydei’s strong thighs, how they feel, how his touch makes Mydei react, how -

“Rule number 4,” Mydei’s voice jolts him out of his reverie.

“There’s more?” Phainon asks dumbly before he can think twice about it.

“Only this one and the next,” Mydei replies, tapping on the page. “Rule number 4 - ask me before you try something new so I’m prepared.”

“Of course,” Phainon nods solemnly, “A teacher must have a class plan in place.”

“Are you even taking this seriously?” Mydei snaps at him, a little too harshly to be a joke.

“I am,” Phainon replies, making sure his tone is genuine. He reaches out, hesitantly at first, but then gains confidence when Mydei doesn’t flinch as he cups his hands beneath his so they’re both holding up the notebook together. “I promise, I’m listening to every word you say. I’m joking, but not about this,” He nods his head towards the list which he can now see.

Its title - ‘Boundaries for Kissing’ - is written in loopy, slightly uneven cursive with a red felt tip, the rest of the list carefully penned in neat lines of blue ballpoint ink. Phainon stares at it for a long moment, heart squeezing so tightly in his chest it’s almost painful. It’s just a list - words on a page - but it feels like so much more than that. It’s proof that Mydei thought about this, took time with it, and cared enough to put his feelings and comfort into something tangible. He trusted Phainon enough to sit down and listen, to take him seriously and agree to the terms so they could continue. And he so desperately wants to - he’d agree to just about anything Mydei laid down so he could carry on kissing him.

It’s sweet in a way that catches him off guard, the list so Mydei that it nearly knocks the breath out of him. He squeezes Mydei’s hands where they’re still linked, slow and deliberate, trying to pour every ounce of his sincerity into that one small gesture. He wants Mydei to feel it - that he sees this for what it is. Not a limitation, not a wall, but an invitation to do this right. Together. This isn’t a sign that Mydei is giving up on him and shutting him down, this is a sign that Mydei wants it, too.

“Fine,” Mydei says, voice rough before he clears his throat. He still doesn’t shake Phainon off, but he lets go anyway, returning his hands to his thighs. “The final rule is that if this ever begins to stop feeling like practise, we stop immediately and talk.”

“Huh? What do you mean?”

“I mean…” Mydei places his notebook back on the table carefully. “If we begin to develop feelings past friendship, then the deal is off.”

Oh, Phainon thinks. The word hits like a pebble dropped into water, rippling out, echoing endlessly in his mind until it drowns out everything else.

Then: Oh dear.

And finally - it’s already too late for that.

It settles over him like a weight, slow and crushing. Mydei says if, like it’s some far-off possibility, like it’s avoidable, like the edge they’ve been skirting for weeks isn’t already miles behind them. But Phainon? He’s been there for a while now. Tripping into it without realising since the day they met, then trying to claw his way back up once he did figure it out - only to find himself falling again every time Mydei smiled at him, or helped him with whatever he needed, or went out on a limb over small things. And now: kissing him with so much intent that it feels impossible to have not fallen in love with him.

Mydei is that kind of person - the rare kind. The kind so quietly full of love that it leaks out in everything he does, not loud or boastful, but constant. It’s in the way he adores animals, especially cats, crouching low to talk to strays like they’re old friends and carrying treats in his bag just in case he runs into one. He never walks past them like they’re a nuisance or invisible. He sees them - he always sees what other people ignore.

It’s in the way he takes care of people without making it a big deal - how he cooks meals for Phainon without asking if he’s eaten, just knowing. How he brings entire trays of snacks to group meet-ups like it’s nothing, like it isn’t the kind of thing that knots something tender in Phainon’s chest every single time. Mydei is the type to remember everyone’s favourites, sometimes without even being told, he just picks up on it naturally. He makes extras, always, in case someone new joins their group for the night. He hands things over with a quiet ‘here’ and never waits for thanks.

It’s in the way he listens - really listens - without interrupting or trying to fix things that aren’t his to fix. The way he puts others first, not because he wants praise, but because that’s who he is. Endlessly patient, quietly present, and never lashing out unless someone truly pushed him too far. He doesn’t explode - he withdraws, thinks, and responds with a sharpness that’s always earned.

Mydei is proactive, not reactive. That’s something Phainon noticed early on, maybe even before he realised he was paying attention. And maybe that’s what shook him the most - how easily Mydei slipped under his skin, how naturally he made space in Phainon’s life without ever demanding it. There’s something so inherently good about him, something calming and rare, and Phainon has cherished that from the beginning. Still does, and he always will.

Far too many have seen Mydei only from the outside: some type of gym bro, gruff and blunt, but Phainon knows differently. Those lot haven’t seen the way Mydei will kneel down to be on the same level as kids and offer them a hair ruffle after they apologise for misbehaving in the nearby park. They haven’t seen the way Mydei offers his module notes out to people who ask nicely, making sure they come with extra post-it notes attached to explain theories further. They haven’t seen the way Mydei gives and gives and gives and rarely takes, sometimes having to be forced to sit down and rest so Phainon can take over.

Those feelings Mydei is so clearly drawing a line under - so matter-of-factly marking as off-limits - Phainon knows he won’t be able to express them now. Not when the line’s already been drawn in red felt tip and blue ink. Not when revealing the truth would mean risking what little closeness they’re still allowed to share. So Phainon sits there, stock-still and forcing his twitching lips to form the shape of a smile, all while pretending his heart isn’t shattering to pieces.

━━━☁️━━━ Moving into his university dorm is already far more annoying than Phainon expected it to be. The lift’s been packed since seven in the bloody morning - overflowing with boxes, people, and at least one kid dragging in a full-sized keyboard - rendering it completely unusable for him. So he’s had to lug his bags up the stairs instead, one at a time, sweat sticking to the back of his shirt by trip two despite it being the start of the autumn months.

Thankfully, his dorm’s on the first floor, which means only two winding flights of stairs between him and a place to collapse and catch his breath. Not so thankfully, his room is at the absolute end of the corridor. A long stretch of identical beige doors and scuffed skirting boards blur together as he trudges past, his suitcase bumping along behind him and his head spinning slightly with each step. It feels like the hallway goes on forever, not unlike a cursed hotel maze where he’s never entirely sure he’s already passed the same door twice that he sees in some horror films.

Phainon is thankful to the taxi driver who’s stuck around the entire time, helping him by half-heartedly passing things out of the backseat and boot so he can drag it the rest of the way. He’s down to the final boxes now, a couple of cardboard ones that hold his stationary and extra bits that he’ll inevitably shove into his desk drawers to be forgotten about.

“Wait there, lad,” The taxi driver says, jogging around the taxi to place his favourite plush of Bubbles the chimera on top of the already precariously balanced boxes he’s holding. “This was in the footwell. I don’t do lost and found, alright?”

Phainon nods, blowing a stray piece of hair out of his eye. It doesn’t work. It sticks to his sweaty forehead, making him twice as irritable as he was just moments ago.

“Thanks,” Phainon replies, hip-bumping the back door shut until it softly closes. The taxi driver clicks his tongue and immediately rips it open again and slams it shut. That’s what Phainon gets for trying to help, he guesses.

Whatever. It’s all done now, one last trip and he can finally sprawl across his tiny single bed and catch his breath. Maybe even take a quick shower before the shared bathrooms fill up with guys he doesn’t even know yet. With that, he follows the cobbled path up to the dorm entrance, scanning his key fob to get in before entering. He casts a glance at the lift but it’s still full, the doors barely closing on the amount of people in there. Phainon shudders at the thought of being trapped in there - it’s probably sweltering with everyone pressed so close and gladly takes the stairs one last time.

It’s a pain to get the double doors to open for him, the heavy wood creaking on the hinges as he shoulders through, looking up at the stairs with dread. Suddenly, they seem miles long, and even though he frequents the gym and works out regularly, his thighs are starting to ache. With a sigh, he begins the long climb once again. Phainon wonders what he’s going to have to eat after all this - if he should go to the cafeteria or order something instead. Both would require him moving again from his room, so maybe he’ll just rest for now and think of something later when he doesn’t feel like his legs are about to fall off.

Phainon approaches the second flight when, with a surprised shout, Bubbles falls onto the floor and tumbles down, hitting every step on the way. He gapes, unable to process what he’s just witnessed, when someone else enters the stairwell, immediately reaching down to pick Bubbles up off the dirty carpet.

“Oh, hey, that’s mine!” Phainon calls, jogging down the stairs to reach the stranger.

It’s not until he’s about three steps away that he finally looks up at the person holding his plush, and the second he does, Phainon almost falls flat on his ass.

The guy standing there doesn’t move, doesn’t speak - he just watches him, eyes warm and steady, the colour of golden syrup catching the light that filters through the tiny window in a way that makes Phainon’s brain briefly stop working. There’s something about the calm way he holds Bubbles - cupped carefully in both hands, like he’s holding a delicate and important item - that makes the whole thing even more surreal. He gently sets the plush back on top of Phainon’s stacked boxes without a word, as if this is all perfectly normal. As if he isn’t casually reordering Phainon’s entire concept of beauty in the span of thirty seconds.

Calling the guy handsome would be criminally inadequate. He’s stunning. Gorgeous in a way that doesn’t feel entirely fair - like someone crafted him from every one of Phainon’s daydreams and set him loose in the hallway to ambush him. His hair is a mess of soft waves except for the thick braid that drapes over his shoulder, golden blonde at the crown and fading seamlessly into deep red at the ends, as though he’s been dipped in sunset. His frame is tall and broad - almost the same as Phainon’s but a little stockier - biceps stretching the sleeves of his t-shirt. And then there’s his mouth - full, slightly pouty, caught in a tiny frown that pinches at his brows and reflects in the curl of the ends of his lips. Phainon has to physically force his gaze to not linger there.

Instead, he gapes. Full-on, unapologetic staring. No subtlety whatsoever. His face burns hot, his tongue stuck to the roof of his mouth, because what the hell? How is anyone allowed to look like that? That good?

“Um, thanks,” Phainon says, voice breaking on the words like he’s a teenager all over again. It makes him flush hotter, especially considering the guy still hasn’t said anything yet.

“No problem,” The man of Phainon’s dreams says, and oh - his voice is even hot, too. It’s low, deep, but not gravelly. It’s just set at a nice, masculine timbre that sends a shiver down Phainon’s spine.

“Are you… moving in?” Phainon asks, desperate to know more and to keep the conversation going.

“Yes,” The guy says, reaching up to pat Bubbles on his little sun hat-covered head. “I have one of these, but in red.”

Phainon wants to drop the boxes in his hands and scream to the heavens. He wants to fall to his knees, grovel at this man’s feet and beg him to - well, he’s not entirely sure what, exactly. Kiss him? Step on him? Marry him on the spot? Maybe all three. Yeah, definitely all three, in any order the guy wishes. Maybe Phainon just needs to do something, anything, to release the sheer emotional chaos spiralling through him like a tornado in a glass cup.

“Cool,” Is all Phainon says, nodding his head along like a muppet.

“Do you want any help with your boxes?” The guy asks.

“Um, sure,” Phainon stutters, offering him the top box with Bubbles on to carry. “Take care of my son, okay?”

The guy laughs. It’s more of a snort, really, a rough chuckle that shakes his shoulders and makes his eyes curve up at the corners and shows a flash of teeth before it’s gone as quickly as it came about. It makes Phainon ache to do something again to make him laugh. Suddenly he wishes he watched more comedy films or stand-up shows to practise the art of on-the-spot jokes.

“I only live on the first floor,” Phainon says as they both begin to walk up the stairs, to which the guy only replies with a quiet hum.

Phainon bites his lip, wanting to glance over his shoulder at him just because he already misses those amber eyes. He doesn’t, focusing everything he has on his shaky knees holding up enough to make it back up the two flights of stairs to the landing. Phainon scans his fob again and pushes open the door, allowing the guy to go ahead of him. He gets a firm nod in thanks and then he catches up.

“I’m right at the end of the hallway,” Phainon says, gesturing with his free hand to the long expanse. “It’s a bit of a pain, right?”

“I’m down this way too.”

“No way,” Phainon perks up immediately, all fatigue washed away. “We’ll be dorm neighbours then!”

“Guess so,” The guy replies.

“Do you, uh, have a name?” Phainon asks, cringing at how badly that came out.

The guy gives him a side-long glance before focusing again in front of him, “Mydeimos.”

“Mydeimos?” Phainon repeats, blinking a few times as it settles in. It’s a strong, powerful, almost regal name that feels good to say. He grins, “I’m Phainon.”

Mydeimos hums again and doesn’t say anything else, which Phainon doesn’t know whether to count as a win or not. They travel to the end of the hallway, finally reaching Phainon’s door that’s already open.

“Just chuck that on top and I’ll leave you to it,” Phainon says, jerking his chin towards the box and plush still in Mydeimos’ hands.

Mydeimos places the box on top of Phainon’s one, hands hovering a few inches away to make sure it doesn’t suddenly fall. It’s strangely thoughtful and it makes Phainon’s stomach flip again. He wants to ask Mydeimos out on a date despite only just meeting, but who knows the next time they’ll meet? Even though they’re in the same dorm building, there’s not always a guarantee that they’ll bump into each other very often, or enough to get to know each other to warrant Phainon’s confidence in asking him out.

“Thanks, Mydeimos,” Phainon says, holding back a sigh at the thought of them parting.

“It’s fine,” Mydeimos waves him off. “Good luck with settling in.”

“Yeah, you too!” Phainon replies, entering his room backwards so he can keep Mydeimos’ eyes on him for a bit longer.

Mydeimos turns around, though, cutting the contact off quicker than Phainon expected. He takes two steps away, and then rifles around in his jean’s pockets, pulling out a set of keys.

“Wait! You live right opposite me?!” Phainon exclaims, eyes wide and hope rising in his gut.

“I said I was down this way,” Mydeimos says, not even looking over his shoulder as he unlocks his door.

“True,” Phainon replies, shrugging. He wants to creep up behind Mydeimos and get a look inside his room, but he refrains and stays put. “I’ll see you around?” Phainon tacks on, his voice going higher towards the end of the question.

Mydeimos pauses, turning around with one hand on his door handle. He looks at Phainon, amber eyes flickering from his face to his hands to his legs and then back up again. “Yeah, see you around.”

━━━☁️━━━

It turns out that Phainon does see Mydeimos around. Quite a lot, in fact. As in, way more than what should be normal, even considering that they live very close to each other. They somehow always leave their rooms at the same time in the morning, playing the game of ‘no, you go first’ and ‘no, you’ until one of them cracks and pushes past the other and then they realise the hallway is wide enough for both of them.

If they’re not dancing around each other in the corridors, then they’re bumping into each other in the shared kitchen at some ungodly hour of the morning. Phainon is almost always craving instant noodles, but Mydeimos is almost always there before him, standing guard next to the boiling kettle like someone’s going to steal it away from him. It took a few times of them doing this before Mydeimos would fill up the kettle with enough water for the both of them, wordlessly offering it to him after he filled his mug of tea so Phainon could fill up the plastic noodle cup he was holding.

Most of their conversations fizzle out quickly, Mydeimos preferring silence over Phainon’s incessant chatter. Every response he gets is measured, brief, like he’s rationing his words - and it leaves Phainon floundering more often than he’d like to admit. He’d always thought of himself as somewhat easy-going, or at least laid back enough to befriend practically anyone with ease. It’s awkward, kind of humbling, and mostly grounding as Phainon realises this isn’t going to be a walk in the park. Befriending Mydeimos won’t be instant or easy - it’ll take time, patience, and effort. But Phainon isn’t a quitter. If anything, the challenge only sharpens his focus. He’s going to get what he wants, no matter how many quiet stares or half-shrugs stand in his way.

━━━☁️━━━

Then it becomes a thing where even in the laundry room, they meet.

Phainon waits until the last minute to wash his clothing, lugging down a giant bin bag full of it. He knows it’s unsightly doing such a thing, but the amount he needs to wash never quite fits into those baskets that everyone else uses. It’s his own fault, of course, and it’s a habit he has yet to change even after a few months of starting university. This time, the machines are mostly full and already running, and Phainon is bracing himself for defeat when he rounds the corner and finds Mydeimos standing in front of the last available washer, slamming the lid closed with his knee and sipping a carton of some sort of red coloured juice. The art on the side of it looks like a pomegranate split open.

Mydeimos turns around and freezes, catching sight of Phainon.

“Rough morning?” Mydeimos asks, nodding toward the overstuffed bin bag that Phainon is very pointedly not looking at.

“It’s… efficient,” Phainon says defensively, setting it down with a soft thud that feels far too loud even above the rumbling of washing machines.

“They sell laundry baskets at reception,” Mydeimos says, taking a sip from his carton. Phainon can’t help but watch the way Mydeimos’ lips curl around the tiny straw, his cheeks hollowing out as he sucks up the pomegranate juice.

“They’re too small,” Phainon replies belatedly, wrestling his eyes to meet Mydeimos’ - whose eyes are already watching him, one eyebrow raised. Phainon clears his throat, looking away completely and down at his bag of shame.

“There’s washers and dryers at the campus gym if you’re in a pinch,” Mydeimos suggests, taking a seat on the plain wooden bench in front of his machine.

“There are?” Phainon takes a seat beside him, quickly abandoning his bag. They’re not sitting close enough to touch, but Phainon can just about feel the warmth radiating off Mydeimos’ body.

“Although…” Mydeimos trails off, leaning forward to look at the discarded bin bag. “I think dragging that thing with you would pose a problem.”

“Are you questioning my strength?” Phainon says, puffing up his chest. He makes a show of lifting up his arm, pointing to his flexing bicep. “I could totally get all my stuff there, no problem.”

Mydeimos’ eyebrows shoot up. “Maybe you could, but I think your pride would take a hit.”

“Now the man is questioning my pride!” Phainon wails, throwing his hands up in the air dramatically.

It gets him a tiny scoff, which he counts as a laugh, which means that he’s won. Mydeimos looks good - too good, honestly - even now, clearly dressed down in a loose-fitting tee that hangs soft on his frame and worn tracksuit bottoms that sit low on his hips like he’s barely put any effort in. His hair is pulled back into a low, lazy bun, though several strands have escaped, curling at his temples and the nape of his neck in a way that makes Phainon’s fingers twitch with the ridiculous urge to reach out and tuck one behind his ear.

They’re still technically strangers, right? Despite the run-ins, shared boiling water, and the way Mydeimos always welcomes him like he’s not a stranger at all even with his slightly icy demeanour, they barely know each other. That’s what makes it worse - how badly Phainon wants to touch him, and how stupidly aware he is that he doesn’t have the right to.

“Let’s make a bet,” Phainon challenges, a sly grin appearing on his face. He leans into Mydeimos’ side, taking advantage of playing around to get up all in his space. There’s a waft of cologne - something sweet and slightly spiced and entirely mouth watering that almost pushes him off track, but he stays true to his crusade.

Mydeimos looks at him, eyes narrowed. “Go on.”

“I bet that I can bring my bag to the gym, and beat you in weights afterwards.”

Mydeimos gives him a slow once over, the weight of his gaze making something fiery sizzle underneath Phainon’s skin.

“And what do I get when you lose?”

“My, my, how forward of you,” Phainon leers. “Already thinking you’re going to win? I don’t think so.” He taps his finger on his bottom lip in thought. “When I win… you’ll let me call you Mydei. How about that?”

Mydeimos’ face scrunches up in confusion, “That’s it? That’s all you want?”

“Sure, why not?” Phainon shrugs, “Your name is nice but kind of a mouthful. Mydei sounds way cuter, don’t you think?” He laughs.

“You still haven’t told me what I’m going to win.”

“Whatever you’d like,” Phainon replies, tilting his head to the side to peer up at Mydeimos.

“I’ll think about it,” Mydeimos says vaguely, but it’s enough to make Phainon agree.

━━━☁️━━━

The issue isn’t dragging his bin bag full of dirty clothes to the gym. In fact, that’s the least of Phainon’s worries now because he’s currently watching Mydeimos absolutely crush him at weightlifting.

“Shit, fuck, damn it!” Phainon yells, watching with dawning realisation that Mydeimos has well and truly beaten him. “How can you lift that much?!”

Mydeimos doesn’t reply just yet, focusing on placing the dumbbell back down on the rack safely, arms trembling under the weight.

Phainon had endured the curious looks and whispers he’d gotten as he made his way to the gym, ignoring them and letting everything roll off of him like water on a duck’s back. But this? This? Is an attack on him personally - to his pride, his worth, his assurance that he’d win over Mydeimos.

“Told you so,” Mydeimos taunts, sitting up on the bench and wiping his sweaty face off with a hand towel.

“I can’t believe it, man,” Phainon says, offering him a fresh bottle of cold water. Mydeimos takes it easily, gulping down over half of the contents in one go. “I thought we were evenly matched!”

“We are,” Mydeimos replies, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand.

“That was an entire 20 kgs heavier than my best,” Phainon explains in awe, holding his hand out for Mydeimos to grab and assist, pulling him up onto his feet. Mydeimos stumbles a little, their shoulders bumping, and Phainon has to clutch him by the biceps to steady him. “You pushed yourself too much!”

“I still won,” Mydeimos says, a devastatingly handsome grin tugging at his lips.

Phainon sighs, letting his head hang between his shoulders as he prepares to admit defeat.

“But you also won the first half of the bet.”

Phainon looks up again with glee, “Does that mean I can call you Mydei?”

“Sure,” Mydeimos - Mydei - says, shrugging. Phainon realises he’s still holding him up and lets go quickly, taking a few giddy steps back. “Although, if you’d just asked me, I would’ve said yes. No need to embarrass yourself in front of the entire university.”

“Ah, but it’s so much sweeter this way, Mydei,” Phainon coos. “I get clean washing and to call you a nickname. It’s a win-win for me!”

“You still don’t know what I want for winning the second half of the bet,” Mydei says, taking another swig of his water.

“Oh, yeah,” Phainon droops, reality sinking in fast. His stomach twists into a tight, nervous knot.

A thousand possibilities fire off in his head all at once, none of them good. What if Mydei wants him to do something humiliating? Or public? Or both? What if it’s something involving dancing in front of the main building’s fountain, or gods forbid, asking out someone on Mydei’s behalf? Phainon isn’t sure he could handle that. His brain spirals, conjuring increasingly absurd punishments with each passing second.

“I want you to test some of my cooking tonight,” Mydei says, bringing Phainon back down to earth.

“Test… your cooking?” Phainon grimaces, “Are you a terrible cook or something? I have a very delicate stomach, y’know!”

“Don’t be a baby,” Mydei says, shoving Phainon’s shoulder playfully. “I’m testing out a new recipe and need a guinea pig to give me an opinion.”

“Okay…” Phainon says slowly, breathing out as much trepidation as he can. “I’ll do it.”

━━━☁️━━━

“I cannot,” Phainon shovels in another mouthful of food. “Believe,” Another spoonful, barely even taking the time to chew as he’s already packing in more. “You’ve been keeping your talent away from me!”

“Slow down or you’ll choke,” Mydei says flatly, offering Phainon a tissue. He gratefully takes it, using it to wipe his mouth.

“It’s so good,” Phainon gestures to his plate. “I dunno many culinary terms, but everything just… blends in really well. Yet I can taste everything separately, if that makes sense?”

“It does,” Mydei assures, then lifts a hand to brush the corner of Phainon’s lips, the touch gone before he can fully even feel it. “You had a piece of rice stuck.”

“Oh,” Phainon says, swallowing thickly past the rice and chicken filling his belly.

Something slow and warm trickles through his veins, so strong and sudden that it’s impossible to ignore, like sunlight seeping through cracks he hadn’t realised were there. His heart thuds, not frantically, but with a quiet insistence - just enough to make him feel it, to know something’s changed.

He gets it then, clear as anything - what he now understands are feelings. Not just a passing interest or curiosity, but something deeper. Budding, delicate things begin to stir inside him. They’re small, barely more than a murmur behind his ribs - but they’re alive. They feel like the first green shoots of spring breaking through the frost, tentative and undeniable, fragile and real all at once.

Phainon sits there, at the shared kitchen’s messy dining table, surrounded by everyone else’s unwashed plates and general mess, realising that this tight feeling in his chest and lungs is a crush. Because, sharing his space with Mydei who is still watching him so imploringly, waiting for more feedback on his food, that everything he feels right now is for him.

He shakes it off with a nervous laugh, the food in his mouth turning to ash as he tries to push past the dread of developing feelings for someone so unattainable.

“Phainon? Are you alright?” Mydei asks, waving a hand in front of his face.

Phainon jumps, plummeting back down to the present. “Yeah, I’m fine.” He lies.

“That was all I wanted to clear up with you,” Mydei explains, and it takes a few moments for Phainon to remember what was going on before he felt his heart shatter in his chest.

“Sure, no worries!” He says as cheerfully as he can, trying so hard to not let anything slip past. “So… waffles?”

“Waffles,” Mydei repeats, nodding his head as he stands up, grabbing their now-cold mugs of tea to dump them out into the sink.

Phainon waits, watching from the side lines as Mydei begins to work around the kitchen. He moves effortlessly, knowing where everything is from their mixing bowl to the bag of flour to the waffle maker, all stacked away in different cupboards and nooks of their kitchen. Phainon was so happy when they moved into their own place because it meant that Mydei could finally spread his culinary wings and buy all the gadgets he could ever need to create masterpieces. It also makes his chest ache, the domesticity of it all, and how much Phainon wishes they were sharing this space in another context.

Not just as roommates. Not just as friends who kiss sometimes. But as partners, lovers, boyfriends.

“I want blueberry waffles,” Phainon calls out, eventually gaining enough confidence to move again, immediately attaching himself to Mydei’s back.

“You’ll get what you’re given,” Mydei replies gruffly.

“Hm?” Phainon grins, realising that his situation isn’t all bad. He presses a quick kiss to the nape of Mydei’s neck, relishing in the little jump he gets in reply and fierce eyes glowering at him. “That was my plea for blueberries.”

“It was a shit attempt,” Mydei says, pausing in his motions.

“I see,” Phainon says slowly, processing. He grabs Mydei by his hips like he’s done thousands of times before, but this time, he uses his grip to spin him around, pinning him to the edge of the countertop. “What do I have to do to win you over?”

“That isn’t what I meant,” Mydei says through gritted teeth, eyebrows pulled as taut as his shoulders are right now.

Phainon knows Mydei enough to take a guess at what he’s feeling. It isn’t anxiety, no. It isn’t unwillingness, either. No, it’s none of that.

It’s anticipation.

Phainon pouts, making a show of trailing his fingertips up Mydei’s sides, eyes following his movement as Mydei shivers. The action pulls up his hoodie a little bit, and when Phainon’s fingers reach just below his armpits, he changes course. They splay across his collarbones, pushing outwards over the curve of his shoulders until he brings them inwards, cupping each side of Mydei’s neck, his thumbs pressed right over his Adam’s apple. He feels it bob under his touch, and then Phainon is moving again. Higher, upwards, until his hands are cradling Mydei’s jaw, thumbs now rubbing gentle circles across his reddening ears. He’s so sweet, so pliant, already relaxing into Phainon’s touch that it makes him want to ruin him.

That terrifying, gaping maw of want rears its ugly head, almost bursting out of him and pouring through his lips as he seals them together, instead focusing on licking across the waxy smear coating Mydei’s mouth. It’s his favourite lip balm, the one that tints his lips even more red than they already are, and tastes vaguely of pomegranate, too. What other flavour would he possibly have? Nothing else would taste this good, this delicious, this right against his mouth. Even inside, Mydei tastes faintly of mint, and of sugar that was in his tea.

Sweet, sweet, sweet.

Phainon holds Mydei still, not letting him budge and not willing to let go even when hands come up to his own hips, thumbing across his hip bones over his t-shirt that he so desperately wishes wasn’t in the way. To feel Mydei’s caress against his bare skin would be an entirely new world opened up in front of him, one that he’s not sure he’ll ever be able to get enough of.

“Have I convinced you yet?” Phainon asks, mumbling the words across Mydei’s lips. He moves one hand again, fitting the swell of Mydei’s cheek into his palm, dipping the tip of his thumb into his mouth, tugging delicately at the corner of his lips.

Mydei swallows, “Of what?”

Phainon feels a flash of teeth against his thumb. They’re still so close, chest-to-chest, thigh-to-thigh, noses brushing and lips ghosting around each other.

Phainon hums, pressing a kiss to Mydei’s lips, then to the corner over his thumb, then to his uncovered cheek. He tilts his head to even press a kiss to the hinge of his jaw, nipping playfully at the skin before he pulls back.

“Blueberries, of course,” Phainon says, grinning when Mydei has to blink himself out of stupor.

“I said you’ll get what you’re given,” Mydei repeats, this time, his voice is thick.

“Sure thing,” Phainon grins, smacking a wet kiss onto Mydei’s cheek before he takes a step back. “Then the blueberries are already out on the counter for no reason?”

“Shut up and go sit down!” Mydei yells, and Phainon laughs loudly, doing exactly as he’s told for the time being.

Chapter Summary

“We’ll make our way through your stupid list, just be patient,” Mydei says.

“Aw, you’re so mean to me,” Phainon replies, pouting.

Mydei barks a laugh. “And yet you’re still here.”

Phainon tilts his head to the side, “Well, duh. You’re my best friend.”

“Mhm,” Mydei hums, voice soft, fading into a quiet that stretches for just a moment too long. He looks down at the floor, lashes casting shadows against his cheeks, before lifting his gaze again, steady and unflinching. Their eyes meet, tethered together, and there’s something new in Mydei’s expression that makes Phainon’s breath stutter. His smile is small, but real, curling at the edges like honey melting on a warm spoon. “You’re my best friend, too.”

“Do you have the lunch I packed for you?” Mydei asks, poking his head around the kitchen doorway and into the living room.

Phainon glances up and rubs at his eye with his fist, “I think it’s still in the fridge.”

Mydei sighs, rolling his eyes before disappearing back into the kitchen without another word. Phainon shrugs him off easily and turns his attention back to the far more pressing issue: cramming an unreasonable amount of crap into his bag. He shuffles his textbooks around to try and fit alongside his bulky laptop case. Still, it’s nearly impossible as every time he gets everything to sit flat, he realises he can’t zip it up. Not to mention he still has to fit in his pencil case and, thanks to Mydei’s not-so-helpful reminder, his lunch box too. Phainon stares at the pile of stuff grimly, wondering if he could get away with not showing up to his lectures today so he can avoid having to do all this when it’s not even seven in the morning yet. He’s not really a morning person, unless, of course, Mydei is making him breakfast. He’d wake up at whatever time needed to eat that.

“Why are you using that bag instead of your usual one?” Mydei’s voice suddenly asks from beside him, making Phainon jump.

“We need to put a bell on you. Why do you not make a sound when you walk?!” Phainon exclaims, clutching at his racing heart.

Mydei gives him a bizarre look and hands him his lunchbox. It’s cold to the touch, condensation already forming on it as the plastic begins to warm up from the air. Phainon places it down on the coffee table, putting his hands on his hips as he stares down at the mess.

“My backpack is almost falling apart,” Phainon explains. “This is the only other one I have, but as you can see…” He gestures to it.

“I’ll lend you my spare one. You’re embarrassing enough as is with your fashion sense to go around like that,” Mydei says.

Phainon gasps, eyes lighting up with an exaggerated glee as he flings his arms out wide and practically launches himself at Mydei, bundling him up into a hug. “I’ll ignore the jab about my fashion sense for now!” He declares triumphantly, grinning from ear to ear as he squeezes him tightly. It’s such a small thing, but it’s basically a gift from Mydei, which automatically means he’s overjoyed at the suggestion.

Also, his fashion sense has improved drastically since moving in with Mydei. If he needs to go shopping for things, Mydei always invites himself along, citing that he can’t be allowed to pick stuff out for himself. Phainon still has no idea what’s wrong with his usual attire and favourite colour combo of purple and yellow, but even Aglaea has passed comments on it whenever they meet up.

Mydei groans and starts shoving at him in protest, but there’s no real strength behind it - more a half-hearted push, like he’s already resigned to the chaos. His hands scrabble uselessly at Phainon’s sides instead, getting a grip on his waist to try and keep them apart that way. Phainon laughs loudly, the sound bright and unfiltered for how early it is in the morning.

Riding the wave of success, Phainon puckers his lips dramatically, aiming for Mydei’s cheek with an obnoxiously loud smooch sound. But just as he leans in, a hand plants itself firmly between their faces, stopping him short.

“What?” Phainon thinks, then grins, slow and wicked. “You don’t wanna kiss me with morning breath?”

“I don’t want to kiss you full stop,” Mydei deadpans, without missing a beat. His expression doesn’t shift an inch as he raises his hand and plants it squarely over Phainon’s mouth. “I can smell it already. Disgusting.”

Phainon blinks once, as if weighing his options - and comes to the conclusion that there’s only one thing he can do. He promptly licks Mydei’s palm. Mydei doesn’t shriek, but it’s a very, very close thing. He jerks back with a noise that sounds like betrayal and outrage mixed together, and Phainon bursts into laughter, unrepentant and loud.
