Phainon wakes slowly as though surfacing from beneath a warm, heavy tide. The world returns to him in fragments, ebbing and flowing in and out of focus until he hears soft birdsong filtering through the window. He notices through a lidded gaze the golden wash of morning sunlight spilling across the bed in long, dappled strokes, warming his exposed feet. It paints the room in a honeyed hue, everything touched by it seeming gentler somehow, suspended in the hush of the early hours.

The colour reminds him of something, something dear to him and important, something - oh well, he can’t remember right now and he’s too comfortable to want to strain his brain any more than he already is. His eyelids flutter open wider with reluctance, lashes sticking slightly. For a few lingering moments, Phainon simply blinks - slow and unhurried - as his heart begins to stir from its sleep-heavy rhythm. With each breath, his awareness sharpens, bit by bit. The weight of the quilt, the warmth pressed along his side, and the discontented hum of the world continuing outside their walls make it hard for him to find the energy to get up.

He lifts a hand to his face, rubbing his eyes with the back of his fist. The sting of dryness meeting moisture makes him wince, although he continues to withstand it to try and unclump his lashes. It leaves his vision momentarily blurred, eyes misting with involuntary tears as he grimaces and blinks them back. Everything feels hazy, delicate, as though the morning itself is asking him to please move gently, and speak softly, not to startle the fragile peace that’s settled in the room. All Phainon can do is comply, listening to the lull of quiet that entices him to fall back asleep. He’s not even sure what woke him in the first place or what made him stir from his dreamless sleep.

Something moves beside him, a rustling noise breaking him out of the final remnants of tiredness. Phainon realises he’s hot, too warm to just be from the little rays of sun and half underneath a quilt. He stills, eyes snapping completely open as he sees what’s been right in front of him this whole time.

Mydei’s already awake, although looking as bleary as he did earlier, watching him with dewy eyes and a tiny lopsided smile on his face. “Morning.”

“M-morning,” Phainon replies, cheeks growing hot as the memories from last night come flooding back. He’s slightly mortified, partly ashamed and somehow through all that he can still feel a twinge of heat in his stomach by the thoughts racing in his mind.

He needs to get himself together. Now. He needs to get out of this bed - Mydei’s bed - before the reality of it sinks in too deeply and he’s left with a hard-on he can’t explain away. Phainon goes to turn over, to untangle himself and escape the warmth that suddenly feels far too intimate, but something stops him. His brow furrows, confusion flickering to alarm as he tries again and finds himself unable to move properly. His mouth opens and closes uselessly, brain scrambling to catalogue what’s holding him back. It starts with the heat - thick and sweltering now that he’s fully awake, sweat clinging to the back of his neck, behind his knees, everywhere. It feels like a furnace under the quilt.

Then he registers the numbness. His right arm is completely dead, tingling with pins and needles, limp and unresponsive beneath the weight of something - or someone, in this case. The static buzzing through his fingertips is the least of his worries once the full picture hits him.

Phainon’s heart lurches with dawning horror as he realises exactly how they’re lying: he’s wrapped around Mydei like a limpet; one arm slung low around his waist, his hand pressed just above the dip of Mydei’s lower back, skin on skin. Mydei’s leg is hitched over his hip, anchoring them together with absurd closeness. They fit together too well, like they’ve done this before, like it’s natural.

“Um…” Phainon says, voice barely above a whisper, unsure what part of this to address first. Mydei’s already spoken, but he’s not saying anything else and he doesn’t seem to want to either.

He dares another glance at Mydei and instantly regrets it. Mydei’s hair is a golden mess against the pillow, lips slightly parted, breath warm where it fans across his chin. His expression is serene, peaceful, completely unaware of the chaos currently going supernova inside Phainon’s chest. Phainon has to bite down on the inside of his cheek to hold himself back because while he can’t move due to their current predicament, he also doesn’t want to anymore. He tells himself it’s because he doesn’t want to disturb Mydei’s early morning serenity, but the truth is far less noble: he likes it. Too much. The press of Mydei’s thigh against his hip, the gentle weight of his hand curled just above his ribs, the steady inhale and exhale that somehow syncs with his own - it’s all far too much and yet not enough.

Can he lean in for a kiss? It feels right like it’s something natural that he can just do. They’re already like this, tangled amongst each other, watching each other - perhaps waiting, perhaps just basking in each other’s presence. Phainon can’t tell because his heart is thudding so loudly against his chest and his stomach is tying itself in a multitude of knots at it all. He doesn’t want to speak anymore, not yet. Not if it ruins the warmth creeping in through the anxiety, or the way Mydei’s gaze softens when it stays locked on his. Not if it risks losing this strange, intimate stillness where, for once, nothing feels like pretend.

“Don’t you even think about it,” Mydei says suddenly, eyes narrowing as he decimates the silence.

“What?” Phainon thinks, then smirks, slow and wicked. “You don’t wanna kiss me with morning breath?”

“I don’t want to kiss you full stop,” Mydei deadpans, without missing a beat. His expression doesn’t shift an inch as he raises his hand and plants it squarely over Phainon’s mouth. “I can smell it already. Disgusting.”

Phainon blinks once, as if weighing his options - and comes to the conclusion that there’s only one thing he can do. He promptly licks Mydei’s palm. Mydei doesn’t shriek, but it’s a very, very close thing. He jerks back with a noise that sounds like betrayal and outrage mixed together, and Phainon bursts into laughter, unrepentant and loud. The quiet, peaceful morning is officially over.

Fuelled by the reaction, Phainon leans in close - not for a kiss, oh no, that’d be far too merciful - but to suck in an exaggerated lungful of air and blow it straight into Mydei’s face with all the intensity of a leaf blower. This time, Mydei does shriek. A high, flailing sound of horror as he kicks wildly, arms smacking at Phainon in a mad scramble to escape the assault.

“You’re revolting!” He yells, voice cracking with genuine panic as he manages to somehow untangle their legs and shove Phainon halfway off the bed.

Phainon’s laughter echoes around the room the entire time, breathless and smug. “You love me,” He chimes airily, “You adore me. You couldn’t live without me!”

“Hardly!” Mydei grumbles, pinching his nose and covering his mouth to ward off Phainon’s morning breath. “I tolerate you. I can barely stand you.”

As if Mydei doesn’t have his own morning breath to deal with, Phainon thinks somewhat fondly. “That’s just Mydei speak for you’re soooo right Phainon, I adore you to the moon and back!”

“Get the fuck out of my bed,” Mydei swears, kicking Phainon’s shin with a surprising amount of force that actually makes him wince.

Phainon pouts, rolling around sulkily. “Your bed is way nicer than mine. Do we even have to get up yet?”

“That’s because I chose it,” Mydei scoffs, finally removing his hands from his face. “If you listened to me when we were picking furniture, you wouldn’t be complaining.”

“I couldn’t afford a brand new one!” Phainon exclaims, huffing and leaning up on his forearm so he can peer down at Mydei.

Mydei mimics him, raising up so they’re at eye level. “I said I’d pay for it.”

Phainon sniffs, “I’m fine with my squeaky bed and lumpy mattress, thank you very much.”

“Just don’t bring any girls home, please,” Mydei pauses. “Or guys.”

Phainon blinks at him owlishly, “Why would I do that?”

“Wh- why? Because… you want that?” Mydei seems genuinely confused, and although Phainon had been excitable earlier and wide awake, suddenly he feels a little hesitant.

“Why would I bring anyone home when I have you?” Phainon says, voice serious, his expression pinched with something that doesn’t quite read as teasing.

The words slip out too quickly, too easily, before he can think better of them - but they’re true. So true, in fact, that they hit him directly in the chest as soon as they left his mouth. Because really - why would he? Why would he bother chasing after anyone else when he already has Mydei? Mydei, who cooks for him, checks his deadlines, reminds him to take his vitamins, and knows exactly when he’s in need of a cup of tea before he even does. Mydei, who kisses him now and then - not seriously, of course, but enough to make Phainon wonder why it couldn’t be.

Mydei is already his favourite part of every day, already steeped into every corner of his life. No one else could possibly fit, even if they squeezed in between the cracks, because they’re full of Mydei too. The smaller things live there, like how he smiles and laughs, each one a well-earned gift. How he talks in that dulcet, slightly gruff tone that sends shivers down Phainon’s spine every time. How he hip-checks Phainon out the way instead of just saying excuse me.

So no, he hasn’t brought anyone home. He hasn’t wanted to. Not when the bar is set so impossibly high by the man lying in front of him, sleepy and startled all at once. Phainon watches as Mydei’s eyes go wide, the words landing visibly across his features like a pebble dropped into still water, rippling outwards. And then, there it is - that tell-tale flush rising from the collar of his t-shirt, dusting his cheeks and the tips of his ears in the softest, sweetest shade of pink.

It’s unbearably cute. Phainon’s fingers twitch with the overwhelming desire to pinch his cheeks, just a little, just to see if the colour would deepen. But he holds back, barely. He’s not sure he’d survive the retaliation - and even more than that, he’s not sure he’d survive the tenderness of it all if Mydei let him.

“My dear Mydeimos,” Phainon begins, a little wry and a little playful. “They’d have to get past you first. And I fear they’d give up at the first glare you shot them.”

Mydei’s face twists into a poisonous glare, lips turning downwards into the exact expression that Phainon was describing. “See! If you pulled that face at them, they’d run for the hills. How do you survive looking in the mirror?”

“HKS!” Mydei curses, shoving Phainon fully off the bed.

“Ouch!” Phainon whines, hitting the floor with an extraordinary thud. “You absolute brute!”

“You deserved that and you know it,” Mydei says sourly, getting up from his side of the bed gracefully, because he wasn’t shoved off like Phainon, and walks towards his en-suite. “Go and get ready for your classes.”

“Mydei!” Phainon leaps up and crawls across the bed to try and chase after him, but before he can stand up straight the bathroom door has been slammed shut and the sound of the lock echoes around the room.

“And don’t forget to brush your teeth!” Mydei calls through the door, slightly muffled.

Phainon gives the door the middle finger and storms out of Mydei’s room, heading for the main bathroom to do just that.

They both step out of their rooms at the exact same time, as if summoned by the same invisible thread. Phainon freezes mid-step, as does Mydei, and they stare each other down like it’s a duel at dawn; both poised and both glaring from afar. Phainon thinks with a fraction of amusement that this is the kind of synchronised irritation only roommates - or something more complicated if you add in their mess of kissing - could master.

“Does your breath still stink?” Mydei asks, tone flat but eyes gleaming with something sharper, almost amused.

“Why? You still wanna kiss me that badly?” Phainon shoots back immediately, a smug grin already tugging at the corners of his mouth as he leans casually against the doorframe, arms crossed.

Mydei’s eyes narrow, his brows knitting together, lips pursed. He crosses his own arms over his chest, mirroring the stance with slow, deliberate defiance. “I was more focused on the question of whether you deserve breakfast or not.”

Phainon gasps, not with offence but with glee. His stomach suddenly responds to the suggestion with a loud gurgle, making Mydei huff a laugh. “I brushed my teeth twice! Can we have pancakes? Do we have time? Please?” He babbles, practically bouncing on the balls of his feet, every word tripping over the last.

Mydei, still standing his ground, doesn’t respond immediately - but there’s the faintest twitch at the corner of his lips like he’s trying not to smile. He gives in though, the smile flourishing into something small yet precious as he rolls his eyes and loosens his arms.

“Fine. But you’re mixing the batter this time. I’m not doing all the work just because you fluttered your eyelashes.”

Phainon beams like he’s won the lottery. “You say that like my eyelashes aren’t incredibly effective.” He spins on his heels before Mydei can reply, already heading for the kitchen.

Mydei follows him with less enthusiasm but a noticeable lack of protest, brushing past Phainon to open the cupboard and pull out the mixing bowl. It’s the one Mydei always uses, the one Phainon accidentally dropped in the sink and chipped the rim. He insisted they throw it away and replace it after a rather lengthy apology, but Mydei had only waved him off and kept using it after that. Phainon isn’t entirely sure why, yet he has no desire to truly dig into it.

“Flour,” Mydei says, sliding the bag across the counter with a sureness that makes Phainon panic that it’s going to slide right off. He catches it quickly, putting it to a stop, and notices it’s left a dusting of white behind it. “You know where the rest is.”

“Of course I do, I literally live here,” Phainon mutters, yanking open drawers for utensils and pretending to search for the baking powder like Mydei didn’t already organise the cupboard alphabetically last month. It’s right where he knew it’d be, but he can see Mydei out of the corner of his eye getting more and more impatient at his delay.

“Why don’t you go grab our aprons? I’m not changing again before class if I get flour on my shirt…” Phainon suggests, pointing toward the wall next to the light switch where their aprons hang side-by-side.

His is a soft, powdery blue with a tiny embroidered egg on the chest - sunny side up, his favourite - while Mydei’s is a pastel pink with a stitched cat curled up in a teacup in the centre. They’d bought them on a whim during a late-night online shopping spree, half-joking and half-serious. Now, they wore them more often than they cared to admit.

“Bossy,” Mydei says under his breath but grabs them anyway, tossing the blue one so it lands over Phainon’s head, making him splutter in surprise and yank it off so he can turn and glare.

“You’re in such a mood today,” Phainon replies, hooking the strap over his head before tying the ribbons around his waist, doubling over so it sits nice and snug. He waves Mydei over, who’s already turned around so Phainon can do his up in a big bow.

“Try waking up with someone’s stinky breath in your face,” Mydei says flatly.

“I did,” Phainon pokes Mydei in the back, laughing when his whole body jolts and a small noise escapes him. “Your breath stank too.”

“Shut your mouth,” Mydei says back, elbowing Phainon out of the way so he can get the rest of the ingredients out of the cupboards. Phainon rolls his eyes, already used to this sort of stuff happening. Mydei will tell him to do one thing, then moments later just do it himself because Phainon ‘wasn’t doing it right’, or ‘you’re not doing it fast enough’.

After that, they fall into a rhythm quickly. It’s not quiet - Phainon chatters constantly, debating whether chocolate chips would ruin the integrity of the pancake, and Mydei grunts in response while measuring out milk with the precision of a chemist. It works for them; it always does. Mydei cracks the eggs and Phainon whisks. Mydei flips the first pancake with an unnecessary flourish, to which Phainon claps mockingly while secretly being impressed.

The kitchen fills with soft sounds: the low hiss of batter hitting the hot pan, the occasional clink of cutlery, and the roiling boil of the kettle going behind them. Phainon’s content enough to remain in silence now, working in tandem with Mydei to get their breakfast plated up as quickly as possible as his stomach continued to growl. Their shoulders brush, feet bumping as they move around each other in a seamless to-and-fro.

Phainon holds the serving plate steady, tilted slightly so the next pancake can slide right off the spatula. His eyes are fixated on the golden brown discs, wide with excitement as Mydei just flicks his wrist with expert ease and lets the pancake land with a light thump beside the others. Steam curls upward from them all, warming Phainon’s face as he leans in to sniff them. They smell fantastic: warm, sweet and delicious. Even without cutting into them, Phainon knows they’ll be fluffy and pillowy inside too.

Mydei’s acting far too serious for someone flipping pancakes. His brow is furrowed in what Phainon can only assume is determination. Mydei’s lips are thinned out ever so slightly, and - he swears the universe is mocking him - his tongue pokes out just a little from the corner of his lips as if the culinary stakes couldn’t be higher and this level of concentration is needed.

He’s so focused, so unaware of what he’s doing to Phainon by simply existing in the same room like this, wearing a ridiculous pink apron over his rugby uniform and looking unfairly beautiful in the morning light streaming in through the kitchen windows. He must have practise today, considering he’s wearing those insanely tight t-shirt and tiny shorts combo, his muscles on full display and tattoos almost glowing in the sun. The uniform is red and black striped with golden thread embroidered through the hems. It clashes awfully with his apron, but it’s still the cutest thing Phainon’s ever seen. And the hottest.

Phainon swallows hard, the motion rough and catching in his throat. His grip on the plate wobbles slightly before he manages to set it down on the counter, trying to pass it off as nothing when Mydei glances at him out of the corner of his eye. But his hands feel clammy now, and there’s a sharp, fluttery panic pressing against his ribs - an ache that has nothing to do with hunger, and all to do with Mydei.

It’s only the tip of his tongue. A sliver of pink, harmless in theory, yet somehow enough to send Phainon spiralling. He has the sudden, reckless urge to reach out, grab Mydei by the front of that silly cat-covered apron, and kiss the concentration right off his face. Long and deep, messy and wet, all until that furrow smooths out and Mydei’s hands aren’t on the frying pan anymore - they’re on him. Just like last night, where Mydei was everywhere. On top of him, hair falling around them like a golden curtain, his face slack with pleasure as saliva trailed down his chin. His hands, desperate and flighty, needing to hold onto Phainon as they rocked their hips together until -

Phainon’s stomach gurgles loudly, snapping him out of it. Startled, he slaps a hand over it, as if he can physically silence his body’s treasonous impulses. His face burns hotter than the hob’s flames, and he’s glad that Mydei hasn’t seemed to notice his odd reactions. He forces himself to look away, just for a moment so he can gather himself. But then Phainon catches sight of Mydei’s expression deepening even more than before. He knows what it means before Mydei can even open his mouth, and he’s sliding the butter over towards him.

“The pan was going dry,” Phainon explains as Mydei looks at him in shock.

“I know,” Mydei replies. “But I never…”

“You got this look on your face,” Phainon chuckles, a low, breathy sound that barely masks the way his heart’s going off like a drumline. He lifts his hand and presses a single finger right between Mydei’s eyebrows, smoothing out the tense little furrow there. “Right here.”

It’s meant to be light and playful; a teasing gesture to keep things from boiling over inside of him. But the second his finger makes contact, something shifts in the air between them. Mydei freezes, eyes widening slightly, watching Phainon like he’s trying to decode him. Like he doesn’t quite understand how they got here after last night, from a tangled mess of limbs to being tangled up in the kitchen while sharing gentle touches in matching aprons as Phainon tries his best not to kiss him.

But Mydei can’t know all that from a single touch. He’s not a mind reader. However, Mydei doesn’t say anything, just stares until Phainon can feel the weight of it in the pit of his stomach, heat curling there like smoke. He wonders if he’s finally crossed the line, that he’s broken out of their brief stalemate about not mentioning last night. He’s not stupid - well, not completely - it’s obvious they’re both avoiding bringing it up. Phainon’s not sure if he really wants to, or if he’d rather let it go and move on to focus on other things. Then Mydei’s nose begins to pinken, a slow flush blooming from the bridge outwards, followed closely by the unmistakable redness in his cheeks. He blushes so easily, so earnestly, that Phainon can’t believe he got this lucky meeting such a man.

Phainon sighs, almost dreamily, especially softly, and can’t help himself when he leans in to press a tentative kiss on the tip of Mydei’s nose as he drops his hand away from his forehead. When he pulls back, the blush deepens, spreading in tender waves like warmth creeping across frost, melting it all away. Mydei’s expression flickers - alarmed, flustered, maybe even slightly scared - before he smacks Phainon on the back of his head. There’s no force behind it, just enough to make Phainon instinctively yell ‘ow!’ and destroy whatever sweet cocoon they’d found themselves in.

“What was that?” Mydei asks, grabbing the butter and slicing a corner off straight into the pan where it hits the metal with a sizzle.

“What was what? You hitting me?” Phainon harrumphs, picking up the plate again so he’s ready for the next pancake.

“Don’t act coy, it doesn’t suit you,” Mydei responds sourly, pouring a ladle full of batter into the pan next.

“What, I can’t kiss you anymore?” Phainon asks lightly.

Mydei hums and doesn’t say anything else, his head tilted downwards to focus on cooking. Phainon watches him in equal silence until all the batter is gone and there are stacks of pancakes waiting for them both to delve into. They’d already prepared some fresh whipped cream and diced fruit, so all that was left was to make a pot of tea and settle down to eat.

It’s not until they’re situated at the dining table, eating their pancakes and sipping their drinks that Mydei finally speaks up again.

“What was that kiss practise for?”

“Huh?” Phainon says, swallowing his mouthful of food as he processes the question. “Nothing. No reason.” Then, he thinks some more. “Well, you were blushing and you looked cute. So I kissed you. Happy?”

Mydei nods slowly, setting down his knife and fork. “Would you kiss me now?”

Phainon splutters, shakily inhaling through the feeling of tea getting stuck in his throat. “Right now?”

“Do you think I look cute now?” Mydei fires back.

Phainon is completely and utterly at a loss. “I - yeah, you do. You always look cute. Can we stop saying the word now, now?”

Mydei raises an eyebrow, “I think you were missing some kisses on your list.”

Phainon matches Mydei’s expression, putting his cutlery down so he can turn to face him head-on. Their knees bump against each other, and without missing a beat, Mydei slots his leg in between Phainon’s so they fit together. “Oh yeah? Which ones?”

“A morning kiss, an afternoon kiss, a night kiss,” Mydei lists out, counting them on his fingers as he goes.

Phainon stares at him, dumbfounded, breath caught somewhere between his lungs and his throat. “Are you trying to ask me to kiss you?” He asks, his voice a little too high, a little too incredulous, his brain not caught up to the situation unravelling in front of him.

“Nope,” Mydei replies, maddeningly vague as if nothing about this moment is beginning to feel charged or stepping into unknown, dangerous territory. He leans in, slow and unbothered, until the space between them shrinks to almost nothing. His hands land on Phainon’s thighs, firm and calculated, the heat of his palms seeping straight through the denim.

Phainon freezes, and suddenly the pancakes in his stomach feel like piles of rotting wood. He can feel the weight of those hands - every point of contact - as Mydei’s fingers splay wider, possessive almost, fingertips digging in just enough to make his breath stutter. Mydei’s thumbs settle near the crease where thigh meets hip, and suddenly Phainon can’t think straight. His pulse is racing in his ears, fast and relentless, the rest of the kitchen fading into obscurity behind Mydei’s steady, frustratingly blank expression.

“I’m just simply telling you about the ones you’ve forgotten,” Mydei says like he’s commenting on the weather and not giving Phainon an unwarranted hard-on.

But past that, past the indifference and past the heated touch on his thighs, Phainon sees it for what it is. A challenge. A dare. A line drawn faintly in the sugar-sweet tension, one that could vanish completely if he leaned in just a little bit further. His mouth goes dry. His heart slams against his rib cage. Because if he kisses Mydei now, he’s not sure he’ll be able to put it down to practise, and he’s not sure if that’s what Mydei wants anymore, either.

“You’ve already had your morning kiss,” Phainon says.

“Really? Is that all you’ve got?” Mydei replies, cocking his head to the side. His hair swishes with the movement, his high ponytail dancing behind him.

“You -” Phainon cuts himself off with a laugh, jittery and almost furious with how much he immediately falls for the encouragement.

Phainon doesn’t think - doesn’t breathe - he just grabs Mydei by the collar of his stupid pink apron that he’s still wearing for some reason and hauls him in like he’s drowning and Mydei is the only thing tethering him to air. Their mouths collide in a mess of sugar and heat, the kiss instantly heated, sticky from syrup and tacky from the cream they hadn’t bothered to wipe away. It should be ridiculous, but all Phainon can do is focus on how it feels - how Mydei melts into him like butter with a soft noise, fingers tightening on his thighs like he’s afraid to let go.

The stickiness fades quickly with a few slow, purposeful swipes of Phainon’s tongue across their lips, clearing the tackiness and replacing it with something rawer, deeper. The flavour of Mydei lingers - sickly sweet and intoxicating as the vanilla cream, overripe strawberries and warm pancakes they’ve just eaten, coalescing into one unbearable, addictive taste.

He’s a feast, Phainon thinks wildly, hands fisting the apron fabric even tighter, not caring if he’s wrinkling it beyond saving. A whole feast, just for him, all for him, presenting himself willingly, and Phainon is starving for it.

“Breakfast is - mmh - gonna go cold,” Phainon manages breathlessly between kisses, the words breaking apart as Mydei leans in again and again, stealing another kiss before he can fully catch his breath. Mydei doesn’t give him more than a few seconds each time, lips chasing his like he’s desperate to feel the heat between them. Phainon can barely think, barely function with how fast his heart’s racing, his chest rising and falling like he’s just sprinted a mile.

He doesn’t know what’s gotten into Mydei today - he’s electric, unpredictable, veering between sharp teasing and soft touches that make Phainon’s skin burn. Hot, then cold. Steady, then sudden. And Phainon is caught up in the middle of it, unmoored and unsure, swept up into the storm.

“Let it,” Mydei says, voice low and hoarse, before he bites at Phainon’s lower lip, tugging at it gently. He pulls back just enough to look at him, eyes molten amber.

“But -”

Mydei then stands up so suddenly the chair legs screech against the kitchen tiles, the sound sharp and jarring after sharing another moment where the only sound was their spit-slick kisses and moans. Phainon’s pulse pounds in his ears, deafening. Mydei’s eyes are wild - ablaze with something fierce and determined. Phainon doesn’t need a mirror to know how red he is, he can feel it, the deep crimson colour reaching from the tips of his ears all the way down his neck like a sunburn. What he can see, though, is the way Mydei’s hands tremble slightly as he reaches behind him to fumble with the ribbons tied into a bow, yanking it loose with a sharp tug. It’s a simple, wonky-looking thing that disappears almost as fast as it appears. He nudges Mydei excitedly with his elbow, catching his attention to gesture to the face before it’s gone for good.

Mydei looks at it blankly until it’s gone, then he huffs a quiet laugh and rolls his eyes, his mouth twitching like he’s trying not to smile but losing the battle. The bus rumbles on beneath them, the world slipping by in blurs of orange light and cool shadow, pressed together from shoulder to thigh until Phainon decides to break the silence.

“Did you bring a list?” Phainon asks, huddling in closer next to Mydei as the old lady in front of him knocks her knees into his. He winces, shuffling his feet back until he can’t make himself any smaller.

“I have it all memorised,” Mydei says simply, tapping the side of his head.

“Show off,” Phainon mutters. “I thought we’d be fine until the weekend?”

“Turns out we’ve run out of fruit,” Mydei sighs, sitting back in his seat and crossing his arms over his chest. Thankfully, now, he’s fully dressed in jeans, a turtleneck jumper and a coat. “And we have no bread or eggs left either.”

Phainon presses the button for the bus to stop, and they get off with minimal stepping on toes as they shuffle through the throng of people who have to stand up.

The cool evening air hits him, and he’s grateful for the crispness of it after being cramped up in a small space for twenty minutes. “Did you bring -”

“The shopping bags? Yes,” Mydei finishes. “Don’t worry your pretty little head about it.”

“You think I’m pretty?” Phainon repeats as they grab a trolley, batting his eyelashes with an over-dramatic flair.

“I think you’re annoying,” Mydei replies and doesn’t elaborate.

“Always a charmer,” Phainon mutters, leaning in so he can tug at Mydei’s braid playfully.

Mydei gives him a long glance and doesn’t say anything as they begin to wander around the shop. Phainon is more than happy to walk alongside Mydei, their shoulders bumping occasionally as he puts items in the trolley until there’s a small pile of food and packets built up.

“Wait, just get the cheaper one,” Phainon says, picking up another box of cereal that’s a knock-off brand of the one in Mydei’s hand. “They taste the same.”

“No, they don’t,” Mydei replies, putting the more expensive one in. “Put that back.”

“You never listen to me when we go shopping,” Phainon scowls, plucking the box out of the trolley to give it him back and dumping his in instead.

“Because you’re wrong,” Mydei responds, sighing gruffly. “And I’m paying, remember?”

“Yeah, I know. I’m just trying to save you some money!” Phainon says while he watches Mydei swap the cereals again, the expensive one now in place. “You -!”

“Yeah, well,” Mydei pushes off, leaving Phainon standing a few steps behind with the cheap box still in hand. “These are your favourite, so stop whining.”

Phainon bristles, face scrunched up in annoyance as he huffs and slams the cheaper box back onto the shelf. “For the record, I think you’re annoying too.”

“You won’t be saying that when you’re eating your fancy little cereal shapes tomorrow,” Mydei retorts, silencing Phainon. It’s true, he knows it, they both do.

“In that case -” Phainon cuts off when Mydei places his hand on his lower back, nudging him into his side to avoid an oncoming customer who’s not paying attention.

They stand still for a moment, pressed flush together in the narrow aisle as the customer finally notices their existence and bows her head in apology, squeezing past them with her trolley until the space finally clears. Phainon’s breath catches, the press of Mydei’s chest against his own sending a jolt of awareness through him. Mydei’s hand still on his lower back feels protective, firm, and close. The lingering pressure of the touch burns, a phantom weight even after Mydei drops his arm to rest beside him again.

Phainon blinks slowly, his stomach flipping at the sheer strength behind the gesture. It wasn’t demanding or pushing, but guiding instead, a reactive touch that’s born out of care. It’s a kind of unthinking move that sends Phainon’s brain into a tailspin. He’s not a small guy, either. Stocky and well-built from years of football, his shoulders were broad and solid as well as Mydei’s. But right now, with Mydei this close, this still, he suddenly feels smaller, like he’s being protected. He swallows thickly, and it takes longer than it should for his brain to catch up. When it does, he realises Mydei hasn’t stepped away. He’s just watching him, amber eyes dark and unknowing, his gaze fixed intently on Phainon’s face as if he’s memorising every detail.

His gaze drifts - slow and purposeful - from the slope of his cheek, the arch of his brow until finally it settles on his lips. Phainon’s breath stutters, his heartbeat jumping as though he’s got palpitations. It’s then that he realises how close they are. Their faces are inches apart, the scent of Mydei’s skin clean and fresh in the confined air between them. Phainon’s entire world sways slightly, and he sways with it, falling more into Mydei as though he’d been knocked over by the passing woman. He wants to say something, anything, to break this tension that’s taut like a rubber band about to snap. He’s not even sure why Mydei is looking at him like that, why he’s waiting and watching and his head is dipping forward like he’s about to -

“We need milk,” Phainon says, his voice barely even a squeak.

Mydei jolts back, eyes going from fuzzy to clear within a matter of seconds. He nods, clearing his throat. “I’m not getting almond milk again.”

“Sure, sure,” Phainon laughs, albeit a bit nervously. He scratches his cheek, “I’m pretty sure they sell that goat’s milk that you like here.”

Mydei isn’t looking at him anymore, jaw firmly set and eyes focused ahead. It’s almost as if Phainon isn’t there, like Mydei has shut him out completely and he’s here alone. He instantly misses the weight of Mydei’s honeyed eyes on him, that syrupy, saccharine gaze that was so soft, so gentle, watching him like he was something precious.

“Let’s go,” Mydei says briskly, and Phainon has a hard time catching up after him.

Once they’re home, things still feel tense. It sets something off in Phainon’s stomach, squirming and panicked. Mydei didn’t say a word on the way back after the shops, even when Phainon accidentally stepped on his toes as the bus jolted to a stop at some traffic lights; he didn’t even bother to throw him a glare or a snipped watch it in retaliation. Nor did he speak whenever he tried to encourage him - blathering on about the weather, his lectures and how excited he is for the sports day that’s coming up in a few weeks’ time. Mydei barely glanced at him, looking away until Phainon slowly trailed off into silence, consumed by his feelings.

Mydei remains silent, clearly lost in his headspace as they kick their shoes off and dump their jackets onto their allotted pegs, moving through the flat with nothing but tension between them. Phainon doesn’t know what happened - one moment, Mydei was fine, they were bantering back and forth like they usually do and then that thing happened where it looked like he was going to kiss him in public. Is that what this is about? Kissing? Perhaps almost breaking the rules he’d set for himself? Phainon huffs, puffing out his cheeks and folding his arms over his chest as he glares daggers into the back of Mydei’s head.

They’re in the kitchen now, organising the shopping out of the bags and putting it all away. Two can play at that game, Phainon thinks as he knocks shoulders with Mydei on the way to the fridge, huffing and sighing loudly as he goes.

“What’s wrong with you?” Mydei asks, his voice on the sharp edge of actually being pissed off.

“I dunno,” Phainon replies snarkily, “What’s wrong with you?”

“You’re the one who knocked into me,” Mydei points out.

“You’re the one who’s been ignoring me!” Phainon replies, almost shouting. He slams the carton of stupid goat’s milk into the tray on the inside of the fridge door. “It was like I was talking to a wall the entire way home!”

Mydei sighs and it sounds tired. Exhausted, actually. The tautness in Phainon’s shoulders holds only for a moment more before he sighs back and turns around, shutting the fridge softly behind him as he reluctantly lets go of his anger. He can never stay mad at Mydei for too long, always too afraid of what’ll happen if he does. Phainon doesn’t want Mydei to get mad back, shout at him earnestly or even worse, leave him completely. He already deals with that enough in his nightmares - Mydei so close and yet so far, Phainon always one step behind and never able to fully catch up no matter how hard he tries. He wonders if that happened in his real life… well, he’s not sure how he’d react or cope. It isn’t worth thinking about, he supposes, because it’ll never happen anyway. He won’t let it, won’t allow it, will never just sit back and watch Mydei slip away through his fingers.

“It doesn’t matter,” Mydei says, rubbing the bridge of his nose between his thumb and forefinger.

“Make me dinner and I’ll forgive you,” Phainon replies, sniffing haughtily and sticking his nose in the air. He slides a glance over to Mydei who is looking at him now, finally, his entire attention all on him. There’s still some fraughtness in his expression, the way his eyebrows are knitted together and the downward turn of his lips that causes a small dimple to appear on his cheek. Phainon wants to grab him by the shoulders and kiss it, making this entire thing go away, but he holds firm for once.

“I was going to make you dinner anyways, fool,” Mydei says but the insult doesn’t sound anywhere near as harsh as it usually does when it’s thrown his way. “But you’re folding our laundry afterwards.”

“No, please, anything but that!” Phainon whines, running over to Mydei and wrapping his arms around him. He brings their foreheads together, squeezing his eyes shut as he nuzzles into Mydei’s face intending to anger him so badly he’ll take it back.

Hands land on his hips, shoving him away. “Then no dinner for you.”

“Mydei!” Phainon drags out the name, his voice pitching high the longer it goes on until he’s making unintelligible noises.

It doesn’t matter if he’s embarrassing himself, all that matters is that Mydei is looking at him again, a small smile on his face and his eyes gentle and fond as he watches on.

“I can’t believe this.”

“It’s your own fault.”

“It’s my own fault that I’m -” Phainon hesitates, holding out the piece of washing in his hand. “Folding your underwear?”

“Yep,” Mydei replies simply, focusing on his pile. “And I’m folding your socks. So it’s even.”

“Not even at all,” Phainon mutters, but he carries on anyway as he folds Mydei’s already tiny white briefs into even tinier squares, pressing them down so they lay flat on his knee.

They sit in companionable silence, folding each other’s clothing and separating them into small piles. It’s nice, being like this, doing stuff that’d be classed as domestic together. Phainon’s never really thought about it before, but he thinks he enjoys doing these activities more than he originally assumed. Obviously doing the dishes, washing and cleaning the flat isn’t his idea of ‘fun’, per se, but doing it with Mydei always seems to bring a smile to his face. Like right now, there’s a small one tugging at his lips as he ducks his head down and tries to work faster, wanting to catch up to Mydei. He’s already almost done, folding Phainon’s clothes with an authoritarian level of concentration and neatness. Phainon bites down on the inside of his cheek to keep a laugh and a jab at bay, not wanting to mess with someone who’s got a hold of his clothes. Mydei’s concentrated face is so cute, all pinched and determined and overly serious.

“Right, these are for your top drawers,” Mydei begins, dumping a load of folded-up clean washing on his lap. “And the rest you can organise yourself.”

Phainon blinks down at the stacked-high piles now neatly sitting on his thighs. He points to the piles on the coffee table, “I also organised your stuff by drawers. I think you’d wanna put that jacket into your wardrobe though or it’ll never hang right…”

Mydei stands up, dusting off his hands before ruffling Phainon’s hair. “Thanks.”

“Not like you gave me a choice in the matter,” Phainon grumbles, but nudges his head up into Mydei’s touch regardless, feeling warm.

“I was sick of looking at it cluttering up the living room. We are not slobs, got that?”

Phainon sarcastically salutes him, “Of course, captain.” Then, he sobers up. “Wait, actually, I think you’re forgetting something.”

“Oh?” Mydei raises an eyebrow.

Phainon taps his cheek, “A thank you kiss to go with it?”

Mydei hums, watching him intently. Then, he swoops down and presses the quickest of kisses against Phainon’s cheek. He bristles, barely even having felt a thing. “Is that it? I’ve been a good boy, right?”

“Phainon…” Mydei breathes out and then shakes his head, a tiny smirk on his face. “You have been a good boy.”

“See,” Phainon cheekily grins up at Mydei still looming over him. He gently places his washing next to him on the sofa and stands up, now almost nose-to-nose with how close they are. He tilts his head to the side, looking at Mydei imploringly. “Plus, you did promise me extra practise.”

“I did,” Mydei says quietly. “But what are you going to do about it?”

“Hmm,” Phainon is still grinning, his cheek muscles twitching with how wide it is. He curls his arms around Mydei’s waist, tugging him in closer until their chests are flush against each other. “I could kiss you right now and be done with it?”

“Where’s the fun in that?” Mydei asks, eyes going between Phainon’s and then his lips as he winds his arms around Phainon’s waist as well.

“I think all our kissing is pretty fun,” Phainon starts, nudging their noses together, lips brushing. He starts to speak again, making sure that every single word is plush against Mydei’s mouth: “Especially when you make those cute little noises.”

He doesn’t give Mydei a second to berate him, swooping in the last few atoms between them to capture Mydei’s lips. He doesn’t deepen it just yet, wanting to thrive off the feeling of Mydei’s lips along his for a few moments longer, Mydei’s pomegranate lip balm smearing all over him. It tastes faintly sweet and mostly waxy, but knowing it’s from Mydei makes him groan deep in his chest as he tightens his grip around his small waist, pulling him impossibly closer. Phainon tugs at Mydei’s bottom lip just to make him whine, and it works, that tiny sound tumbling straight out of him.

“Told you,” Phainon murmurs, his hands moving, moving, moving until they’re grabbing at Mydei’s ass, groping and testing. That makes Mydei moan, and the loose grip around Phainon’s waist becomes like a death knot, tight and inescapable.

“I’ll rate you an F if you keep messing around,” Mydei says, glowering. His eyes are so bright this close, his golden eyelashes framing them like a portrait in an art museum.

“That’d -” Phainon kisses Mydei again, swiping his tongue to taste more of his lip balm. “Be -” He goes again, kissing the side of his mouth, trailing his lips up to Mydei’s cheek. “Awful.” He finishes, landing another chaste kiss against the swell, leaving a smudge of translucent red behind.

Mydei looks taken aback, breathless and slightly impressed all at once. “And yet you’ve stopped again?”

“You’re not teaching me anything, what am I supposed to do?” Phainon replies, putting on a drag to his words to sound bored.

“Kiss me again,” Mydei instructs. “Hard.”

Phainon laughs, slightly hysterically, his cock twitching as he dives right back in, pushing their lips together so hard that their teeth clack. It doesn’t deter him, instead encouraging him to draw back slightly to do it all over again. Mydei shifts in his stance, leaning more into him, his entire body weight counting on Phainon to keep him up. He sighs happily through his nose as Mydei unravels one of his arms to cup Phainon’s jawline and angle him just slightly to the left, taking and taking and taking all that he wants along with it. He goes willingly, not fighting against the demand as he goes. Phainon feels dizzy, overwrought and overly warm, pushing and pulling against Mydei’s lips until they’re spit-slick and swollen from how long they’ve been kissing.

“Is it still an F?” Phainon asks, nosing at Mydei as he speaks.

“U for ungraded,” Mydei replies, voice velvety smooth. “Now get your paws off my ass.”

“Woof,” Phainon imitates and lets go of Mydei’s ass, waiting for Mydei to let go of him. “Are you going to keep clinging onto me all night?”

“You’re the clingy one,” Mydei scowls and lets go, immediately grabbing his pile of laundry, heading off and taking it with him into his room and leaving Phainon on his own. He’s fighting off a smile and the urge to kick his legs out at the kissing, but he barely reels himself in when he remembers how Mydei heard him before doing nonsense like that in his room. He doesn’t need any more embarrassment added to his plate. He stands up and balances all his washing on top of each other, blindly making his way back to his bedroom so he can dump it on his desk to deal with later. He was not in the mood to put it away right now, even though Mydei had already sorted it out into which drawers it needed to go into.

Instead, he grabs a fresh pair of joggers and a worn band tee from the pile and changes, settling into bed and scrolling on his phone. He sighs, already tapping on Castorice’s text chat to message her.

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"Go on a date with me." He wants to say. "Let me kiss you and let me mean it properly." He wants to say. "I love you." He wants to say.

Chapter Notes
