Except, asking Mydei out on a date sounds easier in his head than doing it in real life.

Phainon doesn't have much time—just a few days before the film starts showing—but every ounce of confidence he's built up seems to vanish the moment he tries to speak. He rehearses lines in his head, imagines the conversation going smoothly, but when he's actually standing there, in front of Mydei, words fail him. More than once, he opens his mouth with a hesitant "Hey, Mydei—" only to falter halfway through. The air always feels too heavy with his own expectations, the silence of his fumbling too sharp for him to handle. So with a laugh, he changes the topic and says something safer instead: weather, schedules, anything but what he actually wants to say. Each time the words get caught between his heart and his throat, and each time Mydei gives him a sharp glare that is all too knowing for his liking.

As much as Phainon wants to forget about it after all his mess-ups, he stays awake at night replaying them, thinking of how close he finally got before he chickened out. Because that's what he's doing—being a chicken. He's so caught up on it being a 'date' that nothing else seems to matter, completely losing every bit of his rationality and confidence.

So by Friday, the day before the showing, his chest feels stuffy and his stomach is in knots. The thought of never asking, of letting the chance he has slip through his fingers completely, aches more than the fear ever does.

It's Friday evening now. Classes have been attended, dinner has been eaten, and now they've been left to their own devices. He should be studying, but he's so restless with these burning questions that he can't settle. Instead, he chooses to track Mydei down. He's not in his room, nor in the living room, but he hears the quiet tac tac tac of fingertips on a keyboard coming from the kitchen. He wanders over, clearing his throat when he reaches the doorway.

"Hey, Mydei," Phainon begins. It should sound like a greeting, but his voice tilts up at the end into a question.

He only has today and tomorrow left to ask him out. The tickets are already booked—the confirmation email sitting pristine in his inbox, still unopened. Mydei looks up from his laptop, his eyebrows furrowed and mouth pinched and—

Oh.

He's wearing glasses tonight. Just like that, Phainon's thoughts derail completely. Whatever thread of courage he'd been clinging to unravels in an instant. The words he means to say dissolve on his tongue, replaced by something helpless and dizzying. There's something so unfair about it— how Mydei can look so effortlessly good, how the glasses soften his face and draw attention to the small details Phainon never lets himself linger on for too long in fear of being disarmed: the curve of his mouth, the crease between his brows, the way his eyes—sharp, thoughtful, slightly irritated— catch the light behind the lenses.

Phainon tries to look away, but his chest tightens. It's ridiculous how one simple thing can undo him like this. He should be used to seeing Mydei in glasses by now, but he doesn't think he'll ever get used to it. He's supposed to be asking Mydei to the cinema, not staring at him like some lovesick fool —no matter how much he is one. Gods, he can't help it. There's a warmth blooming behind his ribs, spreading through him like sunlight and static. He forces himself to breathe, to think of the tickets waiting in his inbox, the countdown ticking away in his head. Two days. Two days to stop tripping and blustering over his feelings long enough to just say something.

Yet right now, with Mydei sitting there—glasses perched high on his nose, looking up at him with that sliver of curiosity mixed in with annoyance— Phainon can't remember what words are supposed to sound like.

"What?" Mydei finally says, breaking the silence between them. He's clearly irritated at being disturbed, which should make Phainon feel bad, but it doesn't. He's just happy he gets to see Mydei like this—dressed down in nothing but a loose t-shirt and boxer shorts.

"Nothing," Phainon replies hastily, and then chuckles nervously as he glides over to the fridge to open it. He stares into the shelves and the food, eyes ghosting over the tubs of leftovers and the carton of milk that's going to go off soon, and finds himself spending far too long looking inside, considering he's not hungry or thirsty.

"What on earth are you doing? You'll let all the cold air out!" Mydei snaps at him.

Phainon startles and slams the fridge door shut. "Sorry."

"Something's wrong," Mydei accuses, turning around in his chair so he's facing Phainon fully.

"Nothing's wrong!"

"You're a shit liar, Phainon."

"Rude, I'm not that bad…"

"So you admit that you're lying?" Mydei asks, eyebrow raising.

"I did no such thing!" Phainon retorts, scoffing.

Mydei rolls his eyes and pushes his glasses up his nose. "Either tell me what's going on or go away. I'm trying to concentrate."

Phainon rests his hip against the counter and folds his arms over his chest, trying to appear as nonchalant as he can. It doesn't help the stirring in his chest nor the nerves that wrap around his ribcage like vines. "Do you want to—" go on a date with me almost spills out, but he chokes on his own spit instead and ends up practically hacking up a lung with how startled he is.

Mydei watches him for a few moments before he gets up and rushes over, patting (read: smacking) him on the back to help him catch his breath. So much for nonchalant, huh? He thinks.

"What the hell is wrong with you?!" Mydei exclaims when Phainon finally calms down, his choking simmering down into small huffs of breath that occasionally hitch. His throat feels tight and sore, and his chest is faring any better.

Phainon's eyes are watery, and his lungs are constricting like he's just run a marathon, so he blurts out: "Go see a film with me."

"Are you fucking serious? That was it?" Mydei asks incredulously.

"Is that a yes or a no?" Phainon replies pitifully.

"It's a yes, you dolt. Obviously, I'll go see a film with you. What one is it?"

"Um," Phainon stands up straight again, his back aching from where he was hunched over for so long coughing. He winces slightly, embarrassment colouring his cheeks. "City of Warriors."

Mydei's face changes then—just moments ago, it had been pinched and confused from the choking debacle, but now it softens, opens. His lips part slightly, his eyes go wide, and for a second, it's as if all the light in the room has gathered there, glinting in those amber eyes. "You got tickets for it?" He breathes, voice somewhere between disbelief and delight.

Phainon blinks, momentarily forgetting how to function again. He hadn't expected this kind of reaction—not the sudden brightness, not the way Mydei's whole face comes alive with it. He knew Mydei liked the film, sure. It was his favourite, of course. But this—this is different. This is pure, unguarded joy. And damn, is it beautiful. He's never quite seen him like this before—except maybe when they pass a stray cat on their walks and Mydei crouches down, voice soft and coaxing, eyes full of quiet wonder as he's always bestowed the chance to pet the cats. There's something so disarming about it, this childlike spark that slips past all of Phainon's defences.

He can feel his chest tightening, warmth blooming where nervousness used to sit. For a fleeting moment, he forgets about how he just humiliated himself over asking Mydei out (although he technically didn't state that it was a date…), but at least Mydei had said yes. Seeing Mydei this happy makes all his earlier turmoil and fumbling totally worth it.

Maybe he underestimated how much the film means to him. Or maybe, he just underestimated how much he loves seeing Mydei light up like this. That's why he booked the tickets, right? To see Mydei hopefully smile at him, regard him warmly and with fondness that he can see from a mile away.

"Yep, I bought them the other day."

"When? What time?" Mydei asks in a rush.

"Saturday at 10 PM. I know it's late, but…" He shrugs.

"Don't care," Mydei replies. There's a small smile playing at the corner of his lips. "I thought something was seriously wrong then. You almost scared me."

Phainon laughs, each ha ha ha coming out stiff. "I just… I dunno, I was thinking of something else."

"Oh?" And there it is again—that pinched look, almost sour.

"Doesn't matter," Phainon says quickly. "Anyway, I'll see you then?"

"You'll see me before that, silly," Mydei chides softly, flicking Phainon gently in the forehead. Then, he leans in, pressing a kiss right over the spot he just hit. "Thanks."

"F-for what?" Phainon stutters, reaching a hand up to block off his forehead in shock.

"For getting me tickets."

"I got us tickets, I'm coming with!"

"I know. But why? You hate City of Warriors."

"I don't hate it…" Phainon bites down on the inside of his cheek. Now, that is a lie. He thinks it's the most boring thing on the planet—just a bunch of sweaty, grimy men in sparse military outfits running around declaring war on different nations with some haphazard romance plot chucked in mid-way through. Phainon's sure it's only so they can meet their 'hot female lead' quota in what would be a sausage fest of a film. But Mydei likes it, and he always gets teary-eyed at the end when the main character loses his best friend to an arrow through the heart because he didn't have armour on that time. So, it's not all bad, he supposes. It's quite cute, in fact.

"Liar," Mydei says quietly and then presses another kiss over Phainon's hand, which is still on his forehead. It tickles, making tingles go up his spine and down his arms. He shivers a little. "Are you cold?"

"No," Phainon answers. "It's ticklish when you kiss me there."

"Really?" And even behind his glasses, Mydei's eyes are alight with mischief.

"Don't even think about it—"

Mydei cuts him off before he can say anything more, leaning in to press another kiss to Phainon's hand—right over his knuckles this time. The touch is soft, delicate. It sends a flicker of warmth up Phainon's arm, settling somewhere deep in his chest where it begins to glow. Then, Mydei's lips wander lower, brushing over the arch of his brows, then down across his lashes. The sensation is so light, so impossibly careful, that Phainon doesn't dare to breathe. Each kiss feels like it could shatter him at any moment if he decided to move too quickly—like the fragile beat of a butterfly's wings against his skin that'd decided to trust him.

By the time Mydei reaches his cheekbones, Phainon's pulse is a drumbeat in his ears. Mydei pauses there, close enough that his breath fans against Phainon's face, warm and trembling. Then he presses a smattering of feather-light kisses along the curve of his cheeks, each one slower, surer, until Phainon's whole body feels caught between wanting to melt into the touch and wanting to move closer.

It's almost unbearable. It's so gentle, so delicate, so sweet and kind that it twists everything up inside of him, his heart straining against his ribs. Every breath catching, awe and longing, words right on the tip of his tongue that he wants to speak into existence, but even now, being disarmed like this, he still can't risk it.

"Go on a date with me." He wants to say. "Let me kiss you and let me mean it properly." He wants to say. "I love you." He wants to say.

Instead, a giggle escapes him at the ticklish sensation, and then it's all over. He's laughing, wriggling around from being pinned by Mydei against the lip of the counter top. It digs in uncomfortably into his back, but he doesn't mind, too caught up with Mydei Mydei Mydei to really care. Phainon moves his hand from his forehead and grabs Mydei by the waist, digging his fingers in and scratching over the thin t-shirt he has on. That makes Mydei yelp, his body angling sideways to get away from him, but now it's payback time.

The room fills with laughter and half-formed protests, their words lost in the chaos of a full-blown tickle war. Mydei tries to dodge away and take a step back, but Phainon is quicker; he catches him around the waist, pulling him back just as Mydei squirms and twists in his arms. They're both laughing so hard it's difficult to breathe, their movements clumsy and desperate as they paw at each other. Phainon's face aches with his smile, his chest feeling concave with how little air he's breathing in. He loves being like this with Mydei; he adores it, where there are no barriers between them and nothing stopping them from laughing until their sides ache and they're lightheaded.

Mydei's laugh is deep and rich—full-bodied, the kind that warms his chest from the inside out. It reminds Phainon of slow mornings and coffee that tastes a little too good to rush. There's something so alive in it, something effortless and unguarded. His face glows with it, his glasses knocked askew, eyes crinkled, and mouth curved in pure, unrestrained joy.

And gods, is it beautiful.

Phainon can't remember the last time he'd seen Mydei like this, so unselfconsciously happy. The sight hits him in an almost physical way— like his heart has stumbled over itself, thudding unevenly in his chest, beating away like a drum. For a breathless moment, he forgets to laugh along. He just stares, caught in that light, grateful beyond words that he's allowed this close to witness this version of Mydei that the rest of the world doesn't get to see.

He doesn't even notice how the tide has turned until the laughter from Mydei fades away too, and begins to narrow down to the sound of their breathing. Somehow, in all the movement and chaos, they've shifted; Mydei's back pressed against the counter top, and Phainon's hands braced either side of him.

The realisation washes through him, slow and electric. Mydei's still smiling, though softer now, his eyes glistening from unshed happy tears that have gathered at the corners. His eyes meet Phainon's, flickering up to catch his gaze. In there, Phainon can only assume he's seeing a mirror of himself, because all he can see is want. His pulse stutters, and every inch of him is suddenly aware of the space between them—or rather, how little of it is between them. The air feels heavy, sodden and damp, like each breath is pure moisture with the way his mouth waters and his throat clicks with a swallow.

He should step back. He knows he should. But the warmth of Mydei's laugh still lingers between the atoms of the air he breathes, still wrapped around his ribs like vines, enticing him to come closer, to lean in and see what happens. It's like a spell has been cast upon them—deafeningly quiet, yet no less potent. Phainon wants to stay here—close enough to feel that laughter tremble through Mydei's chest, close enough to imagine what it might feel like if he leaned in just a little more.

But he doesn't have to imagine. That's the whole point of this thing between them, the thing that burns and toils and rumbles through him like thunder. He places his hands on Mydei's waist, this time firmly to not evoke another ticklish reaction from him, and he leans in. Phainon captures Mydei's mouth quickly, not giving him any time to think or to breathe or to chase him away. With his grip, he slowly slides his hands up and over Mydei's waist, taking in the contours of his body beneath the clothing. It's intoxicating, the way Mydei arches up into him as his hands land on his ass, fingers grabbing and kneading until they're at the tops of his thighs. His fingers spread like a bird's wings, clutching at Mydei until he has a good enough grip to pick him up and plonk him on the counter top.

Mydei reacts immediately, a cut off moan echoing throughout the kitchen as he wraps his legs around Phainon's waist, pulling him in closer until his pelvis bumps against the edge.

"I need to get back to work…" Mydei says, trailing off as Phainon kisses a line down his neck, fingers now splayed on the tops of his thighs, his fingertips toying with the hem of his boxer shorts.

"Yeah?" Phainon asks breathlessly, licking and nipping delicately to not leave any marks. Even though he wants to—he'd love to leave Mydei a rumpled mess of red, from his blush to the hickeys scattered all over his body. Love marks, everywhere, anywhere, all to show that Mydei is his, all his. He wants people to see them, wants to allow their gazes to linger on the marks that couldn't be hidden, all left wondering what type of person did that to Mydei.

Him, he would want to say proudly. It was me.

Phainon licks a stripe up Mydei's neck until he reaches his jawline, where he presses another open-mouthed kiss there. He's breathing hard, practically panting, their breaths in sync with each other as his heart pounds.

"You—mmh, are distracting me!" Mydei chastises, however, his voice is as flimsy as a piece of tissue paper in water.

"Tell me to stop and I will."

Mydei exhales softly, then reaches up to catch Phainon by the back of his hair. His fingers slip through the strands, firm but unhurried, tugging just enough to pull Phainon away from his jaw. The sudden space between them feels sharp, like a gaping maw has opened up and he's standing on the precipice of it.

Phainon blinks, dazed—half-lidded, breath shallow. He feels drunk on the nearness of him, on the faint warmth of Mydei's freshly showered skin and the ghost of citrus still clinging to it. His lips tingle where they'd just pressed against him, and the ache of wanting hums low in his abdomen.

But Mydei doesn't move. He doesn't pull him back in like Phainon wishes he would, and he doesn't push him away either like Phainon wishes he wouldn't. He just looks at him—steady, searching. The light catches on his glasses, obscuring his eyes for a moment, and when it fades, Phainon finds himself caught in their focus. Mydei's gaze drifts over his face with quiet precision, like he's trying to map every contour, every flicker of expression. It feels like being seen and studied all at once, and Phainon isn't sure which is more dizzying.

"I wish I could," Mydei murmurs, and Phainon barely catches it. He wants to ask for more information, like what did he mean by that? But Mydei is leaning in again, lips on lips, descending upon him like a sunset.

The day of the 'date'—or not-date, depending on how charitable the universe is feeling—arrives far faster than Phainon is ready for. He's spent the entire morning convincing himself it isn't a big deal, that it's just two friends going to the cinema. Nothing more. Nothing less.

But the moment he opens his wardrobe, that fragile lie falls apart completely in his hands, shattering like glass.

He has no idea what to wear. None. Every shirt suddenly feels wrong as he tries them on—too casual, too stiff, too obviously trying. He cycles through combinations until his room looks like a battlefield: drawers pulled open, clothes strewn across the floor, the bed, the chair that long ago stopped being a chair and became a laundry monument.

He stares at the mess, eyes wide as he runs a hand through his dishevelled hair. "It's fine," He mutters to himself. "Just a film. Just Mydei."

Except it isn't just anything, and he knows it. His stomach's been a tight knot all morning, the kind that comes with waiting for something you both dread and absolutely want. It's making him feel even more restless than usual, picking up pieces of clothing to look at them again before dropping them almost immediately.

A knock at his door makes him jump so violently that he nearly trips over a heap of jeans. His heart stutters, breath catching in his throat as he tries to upright himself. He's way too aware of the possibility of who that might be.

Phainon hesitates for a second, then cracks the door open just enough to peek through. "Yeah?" He manages, voice coming out a little higher than he'd like.

Of course, standing in front of him is Mydei, who looks less than impressed even from the tiny sliver he can see through the door. "You're being noisy. What's wrong?"

"Oh, uh, nothing…"

"HKS, you're lying. Again."

"No, I'm not! I just, uh, need to clean—"

"Let me in." Mydei demands, and at the same time starts pushing against the door.

"No!" Phainon wails, pushing back. They engage in a back-and-forth of pushing either side of the door until Mydei finally wins, Phainon's bare feet slipping on his carpet. "You totally cheated," Phainon grumbles.

"I did no such thing," Mydei says, waltzing into Phainon's room like he owns it. He stops abruptly, his feet catching on the pile of jeans that almost ended Phainon's life. "What… the hell happened in here?"

"I… uh…" Phainon stutters.

"Did you lose something?" Mydei asks, turning to face him with a shocked expression plastered on his face.

"No," Phainon replies, scratching the back of his head. He suddenly feels nervous, letting the boy he likes into his messy room. He's shy. "I don't know what to wear tonight." He admits.

"It's nine in the morning?"

"So?" Phainon counters.

"…The showing isn't until ten at night. You have eleven hours to get ready. Why are you rushing?"

Phainon crosses his arms over his chest and sticks his chin in the air, faking bravado as he says: "Hmph, can't I be excited to hang out with you? We barely do anything outside of the flat together, so…"

Mydei looks at him and sighs, reaching out to ruffle his hair. "Well, first of all, you're not going in that." He says, gesturing to Phainon's bright blue boxers with slices of cheese pizza printed all over them.

Phainon flushes up to his ears. "Obviously! I've been told off enough by Aglaea to have a semblance of fashion sense now."

"Right," Mydei says, but he sounds highly sceptical.

"Shut up, not all of us can look like runway models."

"You do know you're extremely handsome, right?" Mydei says nonchalantly.

"What?" Phainon bursts out, blushing again, this time even harder.

Mydei looks unaffected, like he's talking about the weather and not complimenting Phainon on his looks. He almost looks bored, glancing around the room. "Wear a pair of jeans. And that nice turtleneck sweater that I bought you. The cashmere one. Then wear your blue jacket, which is —" He pauses to look around again. "—Somewhere around here… you know the one. Then your white trainers. There, easy."

"I'm not a doll to dress up," Phainon grouses, but he dutifully goes around his room picking up the clothing that Mydei had listed out. It's pretty hard to find some of the pieces, considering they're buried under mounds of other clothing, but he eventually picks out every item until they're all in his arms. "Are you going to tell me what socks to wear, too?" He asks sarcastically.

"Your thick white ones. They should still be in your top left drawer. Also, roll up the cuffs of your jeans. It looks good that way."

"I don't know why I bothered asking," Phainon mutters under his breath.

"Because my opinion is always right."

"Be quiet!"

"Whatever, you're the one getting ready now. If I didn't help, you'd still be here hours later, fretting. Or you'd wear your banana print shirt… again."

"Hey, what's wrong with that one? It's abstract!"

"It's about as ugly as those stupid boxers you have on."

"Then take them off yourself." Is what Phainon wants to say, but he doesn't dare. After the other night of kissing while Mydei needed to finish his homework, he'd gotten an earful about never doing that again to distract him. Mydei still handed it in on time, so Phainon doesn't see the big deal about it, but he'd been fascinated by how red Mydei's neck was the entire time that he was barely listening anyway.

Instead, he scoffs. "I think they're cute."

"Your idea of 'cuteness' isn't to be trusted."

"But I think you're cute," Phainon shoots back, not caring if it exposes his true feelings too much. Surely calling your best friend in the entire world 'cute' isn't all that bad, right?

Mydei stares at him, completely deadpan. "Exactly. You can't be trusted."

"Hey! That was a compliment, the right answer to that is to say thank you, you're cute too."

"Thank you," Mydei replies completely flatly, ignoring the latter half of the sentence. "Now get dressed and clean this shit up." He finishes, pointing around the room like a nagging parent.

"Rude! I'm super cute!" Phainon yells as Mydei walks away, leaving him alone in his room, surrounded by mess.

The day slips by faster than Phainon expects, losing himself in studying and eating whatever Mydei puts in front of him at lunch time. Every hour folds into the next until, at exactly 9:15 pm, there's a knock at his door. This is it. Whatever happens next—whatever this turns out to be—he's ready for it.

Phainon takes one last glance in the mirror, smoothing down his jumper and forcing a slow, steadying breath. Confidence—fragile, but real—flickers to life inside of him, so before he can second-guess himself, he grabs the handle and opens the door.

And then everything stops.

Because standing there is Mydei, not just any normal type of Mydei, but one with slicked back hair. It's neat and deliberate, a clear show that he'd studied himself in the mirror for who knows how long before deeming himself presentable. Even his braid is immaculate, swishing slightly as he shifts from one foot to another. The sight steals every word Phainon can possibly think of, and all that nervous energy he's held inside all day finally simmers to a close.

Mydei's wearing a black shirt, the first few buttons undone to show off his clavicle and red tattoos, and a pair of matching black slacks. He looks… "Incredible," Phainon breathes out. Then he snaps out of it, blinking and shaking his head as he comes back to himself.

"You look great!" Phainon says cheerfully, trying not to let his voice tremor.

Saying Mydei looks 'great' feels like an understatement. He looks incredible —effortlessly composed, every detail perfected. It's almost unfair how good he looks, how natural elegance seems to come to him in the way the terrible hallway lighting casts shadows across his features, only emphasising his strong nose and pouty lips. Phainon's seen him in every state imaginable— half-asleep, alert, sweaty and turned on, even covered in flour from late night baking experiments—but this is different. This is breathtaking.

His pulse stumbles. Mydei isn't just handsome, no, that word doesn't do him justice: he's stunning in a way that makes it hard to think straight. The kind of beautiful that could turn a simple night out into something more, something that feels significant. Like this could actually mean more than just a casual outing with a friend.

And gods, does Phainon want that. He can't help but wonder if Mydei's excitement matches his own. Because no one dresses like this for a simple trip to the cinema, right? The crisp line of his shirt, the faint cologne that lingers in the air between them, the careful neatness of his braid—it all feels too intentional, too intimate.

For a dizzy moment, Phainon lets himself imagine that this isn't a 'not-date' at all. That maybe, just maybe, Mydei dressed up because he wanted it to feel like a real one too.

Or maybe he just really, really loves City of Warriors and is treating it like some kind of red carpet event.

Mydei's lips lift into a small smile, and he looks down at the floor, which then, as Phainon follows his gaze, he realises Mydei is wearing dress shoes, not his usual trainers. He's even got a watch on, one that glows gold and black. His strong forearms are on show too, his sleeves rolled up to his elbows to give a more casual, laid-back vibe that is sorely missing from the entire ensemble.

Phainon has to swallow when he realises he's this close to drooling quite literally over his best friend. Just to be safe, he wipes his hand across his mouth, relieved when it comes back dry.

"You look good, too," Mydei says softly, looking back up at him. "Glad to see you took my advice." He finishes, stepping into Phainon's space suddenly. Phainon's eyes widen as hands come up to his chest, but they don't go any further as Mydei smooths over some wrinkles in his jacket.

Phainon breathes in, and the world narrows to the scent of Mydei's familiar cologne—sweet, musky, warm with that quiet spice that clings to his skin. It's dizzying. It's addictive. It seeps into his lungs like a thick fog he can't see past until it feels like he's breathing in Mydei instead of air. He wants to sink into it completely, to melt into him, to dissolve in the heat and weight and gravity of his presence.

He wants the space between them erased—wants to close it, crush it, consume it—until there isn't even an inch left separating one heartbeat from the other. It's a dangerous thought, greedy and unrelenting and so unlike Phainon's daily thoughts that it throws him off. Because Mydei is brilliant. Blinding. The kind of beauty that shouldn't exist without a plethora of guards protecting it. Every line of him, every measured breath, every flutter of his eyelashes as he blinks makes something dark and twisted inside of him want to worship Mydei.

Phainon's chest tightens. The thought of others seeing this—of anyone else catching even a fragment of this version of Mydei, dressed and shining for him—fills him with a sharp, jealous kind of panic. He knows it's selfish. Possessive, even. Bordering on madness, completely. But he can't help it. He wants to keep Mydei—the one who smells of citrus and cologne and warmth—all to himself. Phainon wants to take this moment away somewhere safe, somewhere hidden, where no one else can touch it.

Where no one else can touch it but him.

"C'mon, we'll be late if we don't catch the bus now," Mydei says, stepping away from Phainon as quickly as he came, taking all his thoughts with him.

Breathing a sigh of relief, Phainon trails after Mydei to the front door.

The bus ride to the cinema is short—barely twenty minutes—but to Phainon, it feels like the longest twenty minutes of his life. The quiet hum of the engine fills the spaces between them, the low rumble beneath their feet mixing with the soft rhythm of the city passing by outside the window. He can feel the warmth of Mydei beside him, close enough that their shoulders brush whenever the bus jolts. Each accidental touch sends a spark through him that he tries (and fails) to ignore.

He's irritated to realise, with a kind of petty vindication, that his earlier thoughts were absolutely correct—people are staring. A group of girls nearby, probably seventeen years old at most, keep sneaking glances in Mydei's direction. They giggle behind their hands every time he moves or speaks, like the very concept of him is forbidden.

Phainon feels his jaw tighten. Of course they'd notice him. Who wouldn't, when he's sat there so prettily, smelling amazing and looking even more amazing. Still, it doesn't stop the faint spark of jealousy that flares in his chest. He crosses his arms over his chest and puffs out his cheeks in quiet protest, trying not to look as sulky as he feels.

The rational part of him knows there's no point being annoyed—short of staying at home, there was no avoiding this. And there's no way he'd have cancelled their 'not-date' over a few stares. Mydei's voice, him beside him, the simple fact they're here together—it's all worth it.

Besides, the girls will leave eventually. And when the night's over, Phainon's the one going home with Mydei. So, technically, he's already won the war.

"Why are you sulking, hm?" Mydei asks, poking him in the cheek, causing it to deflate.

"I'm not," Phainon replies, clearly doing so.

"If I have to call you out on a lie again…" Mydei threatens.

"You look so good that everyone's staring," Phainon says quietly, leaning into Mydei to whisper it against his ear. Mydei flinches back, eyes wide in shock.

"They're looking at you," Mydei says, eyeing up Phainon.

"No way! They're looking at you!" Phainon retorts, harrumphing.

"So? Let them," Mydei replies. He hums, wrapping his arm around Phainon and pulling him in for a one-sided hug. "Who cares what they think?"

Phainon's mind goes blissfully quiet. He snuggles into Mydei's side, totally taking advantage of the situation, but he can't find anything in himself to care. But when the girls turn around to look again, shock painting their features as they take in their position, Phainon can't help but smirk at them victoriously.

The cinema is practically empty when they arrive. He's not surprised, considering the showing is so late, and it makes Phainon have hope that they'll have the entire screening to themselves.

"The popcorn is ridiculous here," Mydei grumbles, eyeing the concession prices with a narrowed look. "Six thousand credits for a large bucket? No chance."

Phainon raises an eyebrow, already reaching for his wallet. "Alright, moneybags, simmer down. It's not the cinema if you don't have popcorn. Ooh, they have salty and sweet!"

"It's daylight robbery."

"It's not even daytime," Phainon retorts, sticking his tongue out at Mydei before going up to the counter to place an order. Mydei follows him, looming behind him. "Plus, it's tradition."

"You can fund the tradition yourself," Mydei says, peering over Phainon's shoulder.

"I'll have one large sweet and salty popcorn and two large sodas, please," Phainon says, smiling at the cashier.

A hand places itself on his waist, making him jump. He turns around to face Mydei, who isn't looking at him but at the cashier.

"Sure thing!" The cashier says, getting to work immediately on fulfilling Phainon's request.

Soon, he's got an armful of popcorn and a drink, having already pawned off the second one to Mydei, who takes it without much fanfare other than a 'thank you'. As they walk towards their screen, Mydei reaches over without a single word and grabs a handful of popcorn anyway. Phainon hides his grin behind his drink, savouring the small victory—and the even smaller thrill of Mydei eating beside him, crunching away on the popcorn just like he knew he would. It's why he got a large size, after all.

To Phainon's joy, they are the only ones in the theatre when they get there.

"Where are our seats?" Mydei asks, looking around.

"Right at the back, to your left," Phainon replies, gesturing to the area with his hand.

Mydei nods and walks up in front of him, taking a few steps at a time until he's reached the back. "Why did you get seats so far away?"

"I like sitting at the back, it's the best view!" Phainon replies, sliding into his seat next to Mydei.

Mydei sighs but doesn't argue further. Instead, he shoves his hand into Phainon's box of popcorn and takes another handful. "Ugh, this stuff is awful."

"Then stop eating it," Phainon replies simply, getting an eye roll in response.

Before Phainon even realises it, they've demolished the entire box of popcorn. Mydei's hand dips into the tub one last time, coming up empty except for a few lonely kernels rattling at the bottom. He scowls, brushing the salt from his fingers.

Phainon snickers. "I knew I should've gotten another one. The adverts aren't even over yet."

Mydei grumbles something in reply—half-hearted and muffled beneath the booming sound of another over-dramatic trailer—but the fondness in his voice is unmistakable. Phainon's laughter fades into a quiet smile as he glances around the theatre. No one else has come in. No whispers, no footsteps, no rustling of jackets or crinkling of sweet wrappers. It's just them.

The realisation settles slowly, sweet and thrilling.

It's just the two of them. Alone.

Excitement bubbles up in his chest, bright and restless, a feeling that feels suspiciously close to joy. The low vibration of the speakers and the soft glow of the screen make everything feel cocooned and private—like the world outside doesn't exist for a little while.

Phainon leans back in his seat, stealing a quick glance at Mydei beside him. The light from the advert plays over his face, sharp one moment and then soft the next, painting him in shifting golds and blues. It feels unfair, how something as ordinary as this can feel so impossibly charged, even if it's just Phainon feeling it.

He swallows, forcing himself to look back at the screen. He tells himself to breathe, to stay calm. But his heart refuses to listen, beating away quickly in his chest without a care in the world. He sneaks another look at Mydei, who is already looking at him. Phainon jumps in his seat.

"What is it?" He asks.

"Nothing," Mydei replies, taking a long sip of his drink as his eyes trail over Phainon's body. Then, he says: "I really like your outfit."

"Because you chose it?" Phainon says, chuckling lightly.

"No, because you're wearing it. It looks good. Nice to see you out of joggers for once."

"T-thanks," Phainon stutters out. He gestures to Mydei, who still looks blindingly handsome even as shadows and lights play across him. "You look good, too."

Mydei smiles, no, it's more of a smirk. His lips curl and widen around his straw as his teeth worry at the tip of it. Phainon's eyes immediately drop down to watch, wishing he could lean in right now and steal them away from the straw.

"You already said that earlier."

Phainon sniffs, "So I can't say it again? You look very handsome. Dressing up for your warrior boys?" He jokes.

"No," Mydei says, taking another sip. "I dressed up for you. Couldn't let you outshine me, right?"

Phainon grumbles, knocking his knuckle into the base of Mydei's cup just to see panic flare across his face as the drink sloshes around dangerously inside. "You're so mean. Now watch the film, it's starting."

They settle back into their seats easily enough, eyes fixed on the screen as the opening credits roll. There's a roar of noise from the speakers as the actors all begin yelling over each other, cheering and shouting as their first victory is secured. For a while, Phainon tries to focus, he really does—but it's impossible to ignore the person beside him.

Out of the corner of his eye, he can see Mydei leaning back, sipping from his drink, lips pursed around the straw in a way that makes concentration a losing battle. The faint, rhythmic sounds of him gulping seem louder than the film. It's maddening how something so small can pull at his attention like gravity pulling him down, not allowing him a moment to float in the air for a while.

The theatre is still empty, the silence between them stretching out comfortably as the film continues to play. Phainon is already lost; they're talking battle strategy now in a tent, fingers pointing at maps as they discuss tactics. And look, Phainon hadn't booked the back row with ulterior motives —at least, that's what he tells himself—but now, with the soft glow of the screen washing over them and no one else around… Well. It's hard not to think about what it means to be alone here, together.

He knows the rules. He has them memorised. But they've already broken so many without issue, so maybe…

Phainon starts off small. Mydei's hand rests casually on the armrest between them, so he lets his own drift over—just enough to brush against it, a small, accidental nudge. Mydei doesn't react at first; he simply shifts, placing his drink into the cup holder to his right.

Phainon swallows, licking his dry lips for some moisture. Then, emboldened by the lack of resistance, he moves again—this time slower, more deliberate. He slips his hand beneath Mydei's, their fingers aligning, fitting together as if they were always meant to. That gets a reaction.

Mydei stills, the tension sharp and immediate. His breath catches—a small, startled sound swallowed by the booming yells from the film. For a heartbeat, Phainon thinks he's gone too far. But then Mydei's fingers curl back, just slightly, holding him in return.

"What are you doing?" Mydei asks, practically hissing at him despite their mutually joined hands.

Phainon grins at him and dares to do more: he rests his head on Mydei's shoulder, inhaling his cologne and natural scent. "Watching the film," Phainon whispers back.

He can feel Mydei's glare, but he decides to ignore it. He hasn't been shoved off, and their hands are still together, even more so than before as Mydei clamps his fingers down around Phainon's. Just to be extra annoying, Phainon snuggles into Mydei's shoulder, making sure that his hair tickles his face. He hears a grumble, but nothing more. Phainon smiles to himself, his stomach feeling as though he'd drunk litres of soda, bubbles popping and shimmering with joy at their position. It really feels like they're on a date, all curled up together as they watch a film on the big screen.

As time goes on, though, Mydei doesn't seem to settle. He's completely rigid and not a very comfortable pillow if Phainon is being honest. Worry starts to bubble up in his stomach, replacing the joy, and his leg jiggles up and down nervously as he begins to rethink their position. Maybe he has pushed too much, and Mydei is just humouring him to not disturb the rules of the cinema. Not like he could get up shouting and cursing like the men on screen, after all. With a small sigh and smile dimming, he sits up straight and goes to drag his hand away from Mydei's. Yet before he can, Mydei clings to his hand, not letting it go even as Phainon tries to shake it off.

"What are you doing?" Mydei asks again quietly, but this time his face is creased in what Phainon assumes is confusion.

"I thought you were uncomfortable," Phainon admits, stopping his struggling and letting their joined hands fall back down to the armrest again.

"I'm not," Mydei replies. "I just want you to be quiet so I can hear what they're saying."

"I wasn't even talking!"

"Your thoughts are extremely loud," Mydei says nonsensically.

"My thoughts are very quiet, thank you very much," Phainon replies sulkily, lips pouting as Mydei rolls his eyes and focuses on the film again, leaving Phainon alone to his 'loud thoughts'.

He knows he should've gotten more snacks. At least then he'd have something to do except from sitting here and non-stop thinking rubbish like: oh my gods, we're holding hands. His hand is so soft, does he use moisturiser? I can't even feel the callouses from rugby anymore.

His attention and thoughts drift again, and he finds himself watching Mydei once again. He looks different now, more subdued, comfortable, more… less, as little sense as that makes. But it's true—even dressed to the nines in his black shirt and trousers, his hair loose and slicked back, he seems so comfortable in himself that he might as well be at home in his loose t-shirt and a tiny pair of shorts.

Phainon knows he's thought it a thousand times already, but Mydei really is beautiful—even more so as the shadows and lights casting from the screen dance across his features, brightening them and throwing them into darkness all at once. He's a film himself, a set of moving pictures that evoke a response in Phainon's heart that he can't just shift and get rid of. He's a film Phainon could watch forever, from the beginning credits til the ending ones, Phainon will dutifully sit and watch no matter what. He's so desperate to not miss a thing that he doesn't even want to blink, even as his eyes sting and well up with tears to compensate, just in case he misses something and the film of 'Mydei' ends.

So Phainon savours as much as he can, not caring that he's being so brazen, not caring that he's missing whatever's actually going on the screen right now, not caring that Mydei is now looking at him with a confused scowl. Gorgeous, Phainon thinks, all to himself. He gobbles it up, eating as much as he can see of Mydei up in his head and swallowing it down to keep for later. He never said he wasn't greedy, because he is. Horribly, irrevocably, entirely greedy for the man before him.

He wants to kiss him so badly he feels his chest ache.

"Quit looking at me like that," Mydei mutters.

"Like what?" Phainon throws back, a little too loud.

Mydei bites his bottom lip, and Phainon's eyes immediately zero in on the action. He finds himself mimicking it without really thinking, chewing on his lip, wishing that it was Mydei's instead. Phainon wonders what he'd taste like today—whether it'd be saccharine, as usual? Or maybe slightly salty from the popcorn he stole. Maybe, even, lemony as the sherbet sweets he's probably got stashed in his trouser pockets, hidden away so Phainon can't steal one for himself?

"Remember rule number one."

Phainon gasps dramatically. "Are you suggesting that I want to kiss you in public, my dear Mydeimos?"

"Don't play stupid. I know that dumb look on your face."

"Oh yeah?" Phainon challenges. "What do I look like?"

Mydei holds his gaze before dropping it, his eyes landing on Phainon's lips. "Like you want to kiss me right now."

Phainon gulps, "Would you let me, if I did want to?"

"No," Mydei replies back quickly. Then he sighs. "Yes, no, maybe. I don't know."

"We don't have to," Phainon reaches out with his free hand to cup Mydei's cheek, relishing in the softness beneath his palm as Mydei leans into it like a cat, his eyelashes fluttering sweetly.

"I want to," Mydei admits, so quiet that the film on screen almost swallows it up completely.

"You do?" Phainon breathes out, and suddenly their faces are close, closer than before, their noses brushing and foreheads knocking gently against one another.

"Yes." Mydei answers, and it's all it takes for Phainon to close the distance between them, pressing his lips against Mydei's.

Mydei's grip tightens around his hand—hard enough to almost hurt—but Phainon doesn't pull away. He doesn't dare to. He doesn't want to. If anything, the pressure grounds him, keeps him tethered while everything else feels like it's spinning out of control.

Their kiss is clumsy at first, as if all their practise has gone out the window. There's too much urgency, not enough breath, just a smashing of lips and a wildness behind them both. Their lips move together until the rhythm finally settles, until their heads tilt just right and the whole world falls away in shattering pieces. Every press of Mydei's mouth against his feels like a spark caught between them, something impossibly vibrant and bright that Phainon's eyes squeeze shut in fear that it might blind him.

Phainon can't think. He can only feel—the heat of it, the sweetness as he licks into Mydei's mouth, the way Mydei opens up so easily for him, like he was waiting for this moment too. Phainon feels wanted. It's a dizzying rush, one that makes his cock twitch in his jeans, one that makes his delicate hold on Mydei's face turn feral, his nails sinking inwards only a fraction as to still them both in time. Something vast has bloomed in his chest, a whole new cosmos, spinning wildly where his heart should be.

They're in public. They're kissing—in public. They shouldn't be doing this, no matter how alone they are right now. Someone could still walk in, even though it's been almost an entire hour since the film started. He knows that, and the thought flickers like a candle in the wind at the back of his mind, faint and useless. Because right now, none of it matters—the empty theatre, the rules, the risk. The only thing that exists is this: Mydei's hand in his, the taste of his breath and the feeling of courage racing through his veins.

Phainon doesn't stop kissing him. He can't. Mydei tastes sweet and salty, exactly like the popcorn. It's delicious, and he can't get enough, especially when Mydei starts making those breathy little sounds that turn him on immediately. Heat begins to pool in his gut, low and boiling and dangerous, and he really wishes they were at home, maybe in bed or on the sofa, so Phainon could lay Mydei down. He wants to be horizontal with him, over him and under him, all over him, hands in his hair and on the nape of his neck and passing down over his shoulders to reach his tiny waist. He wants so much, so much, that it takes his breath away even more as they kiss and kiss and kiss, lips swollen and sore and his heart about to beat out of his ribcage.

When Mydei pulls away, it's as though Phainon's heart follows him, out through his mouth and splattering into a puddle on the floor. He wants more already, needs to keep kissing him until his lips hurt and his lungs ache. He needs—

He stops. He looks at Mydei. He looks…

Mydei looks… wrong. All jagged and broken, his face scrunched up into something that Phainon can't quite pinpoint. Disgust? Uncertainty? Distaste? He's not sure, and he's also not sure if he wants to know either. But he can't help but ask:

"What's wrong?" Phainon asks tentatively.

Mydei swallows, and then their hands are pulled apart, and Phainon's hand is left cold and clammy. "We shouldn't have done that."

"Mydei?" Phainon asks faintly, the name on his lips feeling like a plea.

"We—" Mydei gets up suddenly, and he's storming down the steps of the cinema, taking a few at a time.

"Wait! Mydei!" Phainon yells, not giving a shit anymore about keeping quiet. He doesn't care if the clerk above them streaming the film hears him, or sees him frantically chasing after Mydei down the stairs. He also takes a few at a time, trying so desperately to catch up.

Once they're out of the theatre, Mydei seems to slow down, but then he speeds up again. Phainon keeps going after him, frantic and panicked, not knowing what to do except to keep running.

"Mydei! Slow down!"

Then, they're outside, the cold air hitting Phainon in the face like a ton of bricks. He's cold, shivering, suddenly too warm and too freezing at the same time as his teeth chatter, and he's still trying to catch up to Mydei, who's way ahead of him again. It's like a storm has broken out, a tornado of emotions and feelings twisting up inside of him.

Mydei only stops once they reach the bus stop.

It's stupid, there are no buses for ages this late at night. Phainon jogs up behind him, panting and wheezing as his heart feels like it's going to give out at any second.

"Mydei— what—"

"We shouldn't have done that," Mydei repeats.

"I'm sorry," Phainon says. "Mydei, I'm sorry. I shouldn't've—"

"It wasn't your fault! It was— it was mine."

"Why are we blaming ourselves over something like this? It's— it's fine, right? We're fine?"

Mydei nods sharply.

Phainon breathes out a sigh of relief. "Let's get a cab home, okay?" His voice is gentle, coaxing, trying to sound normal even though his pulse is still all over the place. He reaches out, slow and careful, meaning only to rest a reassuring hand on Mydei's shoulder.

But Mydei steps out of reach.

Oh. Phainon thinks, the simple action hitting him like a punch to the gut. The air leaves his lungs with it, and for a moment, he just stands there, his hand half-raised, stupidly frozen between them. Mydei won't meet his eyes, instead looking at the ground. His shoulders are drawn tight, his jaw set, and Phainon can see the tremor in his hand as he runs one over his braid, a nervous tic he's never quite managed to hide.

Guilt floods Phainon's chest, thick and heavy. He wants to say something— to apologise, to explain, to take it all back if it would stop that look on Mydei's face—but the words tangle in his throat.

"Mydei," He starts softly, but the other only shakes his head.

"It was—" Mydei cuts himself off, shakily exhaling. "We shouldn't have… not there. Not like that." His voice is raw, quiet but sharp around the edges, each word cutting like little knives into Phainon's skin.

Phainon swallows hard, forcing a smile on his face that doesn't reach his eyes. "Yeah. Yeah, you're right." He laughs under his breath, brittle and small. Because it's true, Mydei is right; however, it's still hard to fully grasp. "Guess I got too caught up in it."

A beat passes. The sound of the city echoes around them—the distant whoosh of cars, the low murmur of people spilling out of late-night shops. The world moves on, uncaring, while Phainon feels like his has just cracked down the middle.

He doesn't feel so wanted anymore.

But he wants to reach out again, to bridge that tiny, impossible gap between them. To tell Mydei it meant something—that for him, it wasn't just the heat of the moment, it was everything. He wants to explain that he wanted this to be their first proper date, that he got all dressed up for Mydei and no one else. That he went through all the planning, the painstaking deliberation to muster up the courage to just ask, all for him.

Yet Mydei is still holding himself so tightly, and he doesn't dare push. So instead he exhales, long and silent, and nods towards the street. "Come on," He says, barely above a whisper. "Let's get home. It's cold out," Phainon shrugs off his jacket and hands it over to Mydei, who takes it without a word and puts it on over his shirt.

Phainon shivers despite still wearing a thick cashmere jumper, but it's not the cold air that's affecting him. It's the coldness from Mydei that is. He grabs his phone and dials a local taxi place, explaining to them where they are and nodding along when the guy says that they'll be there in ten minutes.

"Ten minutes," Phainon reiterates.

Mydei just nods.

The ride home is silent.

Phainon kicks off his shoes the moment they get in, and Mydei carefully puts Phainon's jacket up on the peg to the side. The silence is deafening, so much so that it's almost painful. They head into the kitchen, side-by-side, their shoulders knocking as Mydei immediately heads to the kettle to put it on.

The silence… the quiet…

"Mydei," Phainon says, and Mydei turns around to look at him. He looks exhausted, eyes worn, and lips curled down into a frown. "I need to tell you something."

"What is it?" Mydei asks, and he sounds as tired as he looks.

"I wanted today to be a date," Phainon admits, his hands shaking as he clasps them together in front of him, just to try and keep them steady. "I wanted… today to be special. That's why I was so scared to ask you out."

"A date…?" Mydei repeats, as though he's not understanding. He shakes his head, "We're not dating, though."

"I want to be," Phainon says in a rush. His heart is beating wildly, his palms clammy, and he can't quite pick a spot to keep looking at, his eyes all over the place as Mydei stays in the centre of his field of vision. "I want to date you."

Mydei looks at him, shocked, eyes wide and mouth open. There's a flush on his ears, on his cheeks and dusting over the bridge of his nose. Hope fills Phainon, then, irreversible and stupid.

"Those rules we put in place? I've practically broken all of them," Phainon swallows past the lump in his throat. "Rule one, rule three, and five."

Mydei blinks at him, head shaking to and fro as he processes. "Five?"

"When it stops feeling like practise," Phainon steps forward. "And we… I… develop feelings."

"You think you have feelings for me?"

"I know I have feelings for you!" Phainon says, putting one hand over his chest. He can feel his heart beating rapidly. "I know I'm in love with you."

"You're confused," Mydei says flippantly, and all the hope Phainon was feeling recedes like the ocean tide withdrawing.

"I'm not! Don't tell me how to feel when I've been in love with you since the first time we ever met!"

"You're just— you're—"

Phainon cuts off his stuttering. "What, Mydei?" He takes another step forward and grabs Mydei's hands, gathering them up like a lifeline. He tries to catch Mydei's gaze, tries to lock their eyes together and to make him physically see and not just hear how sincere he is. "I've loved you for a long time," His voice breaks. "Please, Mydei— Mydeimos, please, I don't know how else to say it to make you believe me."

"Do you not feel anything for me? Is that it?"

"No!" Mydei shouts, then his eyebrows furrow, and he's biting his stupid bottom lip again, and even more stupidly, Phainon wants to kiss him again.

"No…?"

"No, I— yes, yes… I feel… things for you, but I just…"

"Just what?"

"I need… space. I think we need time apart."

The whole world tilts on its axis then. "What do you mean?" Phainon asks faintly. He feels like he's going to pass out.

"I meant what I said. We need space. Then— then you'll see that you don't know what's going on, and then we can go back to the way things were."

"What? Before we started kissing? Before I felt you on top of me, before I saw you cum because of me?"

"You're so—!" Mydei sounds frustrated, his blush deepening.

"That all meant nothing to you? All our kisses, all the time we spend together, all the things we do for each other. Nothing?"

"That's not what I'm saying!" Mydei yells. He yanks his hands away from Phainon's. "This whole kissing thing was a bad idea. It's gotten us all confused and— and I don't want our friendship to be ruined because we got too carried away."

"It won't— it hasn't— ruined our friendship! I just… I'll admit, I want more, Mydeimos. I always want more. But it's not anything you have to give to me, it's just things that I wanna do for you. Do to you. I wanna, I dunno, be able to hold your hand in public and call you mine and be your stupid fucking boyfriend, yeah? That's not ruining our friendship. We'll still be friends, just with more."

Mydei looks at him, and there's nothing there. Nothing in his expression to show delight, happiness or joy at his confession. He just looks… sad.

"I got it all wrong, didn't I?" Phainon asks, putting his hands over his face.

"That's not what I'm saying," Mydei replies.

"Then what are you saying? I'm so confused right now, I don't understand what's going on. I thought we were fine, better than fine, I thought—"

"You thought wrong."

"Right." Phainon says. His heart feels like steel. "Fine." He storms past Mydei, knocking their shoulders together roughly as he heads straight for his room.

His room is still somewhat of a mess with all the clothes everywhere, but he knows vaguely where everything he wants to grab is. He yanks his duffel bag out of his wardrobe and shoves whatever clothes he can fit into it, not caring if they make any sense or if they're just random odds and ends he can find. He tears into his drawers, filling the rest of the space with underwear and socks. Underwear and socks that Mydei folded for him.

How could he be so dumb, so silly, so caught up in his own little world that he didn't notice how Mydei was feeling the entire time?

"What are you doing?" Mydei asks from his doorway.

"Why don't you use those assuming skills you've suddenly developed and take a wild guess?"

"Phainon—"

"No," Phainon zips up his bag and hitches it over his shoulder. "You don't get to dictate everything, Mydei. You won't accept my feelings, fine. Just say that. But I know you're lying to yourself, too. I can tell. But I'm not going to force you, so you can deal with your shit and come back to me when you're ready."

"Phainon— Wait, wait—"

Phainon barges past him again, ramming his feet into his shoes and not even bothering to get the backs of them over his heels. He grabs his jacket, folding it over his arm to put on when he's fucking out of here. He doesn't want to stay in this place for a moment longer.

"Where are you going?!"

"Away from you!" Phainon shouts, spinning around to face Mydei. He looks wild, hair in disarray and eyes so impossibly wide as his mouth opens and shuts, at a loss for words. He looks panicked, scared and shocked all rolled into one.

"Phainon, please, just wait, I—"

"I'm going to Cas's." Phainon cuts him off again. He opens the door, not before grabbing his set of keys from the side counter and shoving them in his jeans pocket.

"Why?"

"Why?!" Phainon hates—hates—that he's yelling at Mydei, but he can't help it. Not as tears well up in his eyes, blurring his vision and leaving hot trails behind on his cheeks as they seep downwards. "Because the man I love doesn't love me back, okay? That's why."

He ignores the rest of Mydei's pleas and slams the door shut behind him. He can barely see through his tears, searing and hot as they continuously fill his vision, but what he can't get past is seeing the devastated face of Mydei alongside it.
