The walk to Castorice's feels endless, hours long rather than the actual measly fifteen minutes that it actually takes to get there. Every step drags, heavy and clumsy, like he's wading through something thicker than rain. And the rain currently drenching him really doesn't help. It comes down in sheets, cold and merciless, soaking him to the bone until he can't tell where the water ends and his tears begin. They slide down his face together, indistinguishable, just more proof that the universe has some sort of cruel sense of irony.

He almost laughs at the thought—how ridiculous he must look right now. A drenched, miserable mess, wandering through the streets like the lead in some cheap rom-com's third-act heartbreak montage. Except this isn't a shitty film he'd watch with Mydei, snuggled up on the sofa, but his actual life, real and true. There's no melancholic music swelling, no cinematic lighting to make his pain look poetic. Just the rain, the cold, and the dull ache in his chest.

And the worst part? There wasn't even a breakup. There never could be. You can't break what was never whole to begin with—and he supposes that's true for him and Mydei now, so close and yet so far from what he truly wanted. He really had gotten it incredibly wrong, something he never thought would happen has happened and now he has to deal with it. So, he walks alone—soaked, shivering, and silently wishing the world would just stop for a moment so he could catch his breath.

The thoughts make his heart hurt even more, and as he knocks on Castorice's door, he finds himself sniffling and trying not to bawl his eyes out again. It only takes a few moments before Castorice is answering the door, pulling it open with a confused look on her face until recognition clears it.

"Phainon? What are you doing here? It's so late…"

"Cas— I—" Phainon stutters, bottom lip trembling as his hair begins to plaster itself to his forehead from the rain still pouring down.

"Oh my, never mind that, come on in!" Castorice says, grabbing Phainon by his hand and guiding him inside.

His face scrunches up almost immediately, trying to hold it together, but the effort is useless. The tears come hot and fast, cutting through the rain still clinging to his skin. His breath catches in his throat, and all at once the sound that escapes him isn't really a cry—it's a broken thing, torn out from somewhere deep. Castorice's hands are on his cheeks immediately, wiping away the tears as they come. Her face is creased in worry, eyebrows furrowed and lips pursed as she clearly wants to ask or say something, but she keeps it to herself.

Phainon can't take it anymore. Overwhelmed by his best friend's care, he doubles over, not caring how dramatic it may seem, and Castorice exclaims in shock. Her hands immediately drop from his face and come up to rest on his shoulders, ever so delicate but ever so warm, steadying him.

"Hey, Phainon, hey— look at me. What happened?" Castorice coaxes gently, her voice soft and panicked at the same time.

He doesn't know how to answer. Not yet, not right now. The words won't form. His throat is tight, his chest hurts, and his mind is a blur of Mydei's face—his voice, his eyes, the way he looked when everything fell apart.

"I messed up," Phainon chokes out finally, shuddering with the words. He barely speaks above a whisper. "I thought— I thought he… I thought Mydei…" He can't even finish the sentence. The sobs tear through him again, harder this time, but he stands up straight to look Castorice in the face.

Castorice doesn't say anything after that. She pulls him in, arms wrapping around his shoulders as she stands on her tip-toes to reach him. She holds him close despite how soaked he is, and even as her clothes darken with dampness, she doesn't seem to care. Castorice just rubs slow, careful circles on his back, murmuring phrases and soft sounds that are meant to keep him anchored.

It works, at least for the moment. Phainon buries his face into her shoulder, breath shaky, the smell of rain and salt and despair thick in the air. His heart feels split open, raw and aching, but at least here, right now, he doesn't have to hide it. He clutches at her, fingernails scraping over her shoulder blades as he scrabbles to try and gather her into his arms even harder. She's in a nightgown, clearly having just woken up, and he feels so bad that she's here comforting him like this when she should be sleeping. He should be sleeping too, not crying all over one of his best friends.

"I'm sorry," Phainon slurs out, his tongue heavy in his mouth. "You were asleep. I—"

"I wasn't," She assures. "I was watching TV and then I heard you knocking. It's fine, it's okay, don't worry, alright?"

He nods into her shoulder.

"It's okay," Castorice says again in a soft whisper, voice steady and sure even though she doesn't even know what happened. "Whatever went down, you'll be okay. You both will."

Phainon breathes out a laugh, more a huff of air than anything, but it's a laugh nonetheless. He shrugs in her hold, but he wants to believe her. Gods, does he want to. But all he can do is shake his head, the words tumbling out between his shivering: "It doesn't feel like it."

And then he just cries again—loud, messy, unguarded. The sound fills the entryway, echoing against the floorboards and walls, until all that's left as he calms down is the quiet patter of rain on the window and the low hum of Castorice's voice telling him, again and again, that it's all okay.

After a while, once the tears stop and he's worn out, he withdraws from her hold. It's cold, so cold, and he shivers, teeth chattering from adrenaline and the temperature.

"Oh, Phainon… Let's get you into something warm, okay? You can go shower and I'll put your pyjamas on the radiator for a bit."

Phainon nods simply and trails along behind Castorice, making sure the front door is firmly shut and locked before doing so. She leads them further into her house, hand in hand, and guides him to her bathroom. She flicks on the light and gently pushes him towards the shower cubicle.

"I'll get you some spare towels, just wait here," Castorice says as she scurries off, leaving Phainon alone.

He feels it all at once—the weight of being alone. It's heavy, suffocating, pressing down on his chest until he can barely breathe. He fears he might start hyperventilating at this rate, so he closes his eyes and breathes in through his nose deeply, counting a few seconds before letting it out slowly through his mouth. It helps, at least a tiny bit, and his heart rate returns back to normal in a few measured breaths.

He's always hated it—the silence. It crawls into the cracks of his thoughts and fills them with every awful thing he tries not to remember. Every nightmare, every fear, every moment that he's been left behind.

Phainon hates it. He despises it. He wishes he could claw his way out of it by sheer willpower alone.

Castorice means well, of course she does. He knows that. She's opened her door to him, offered him comfort and safety, and he's grateful for it, he really is. But this isn't how things were supposed to be. He shouldn't even be here. He should be at home—with him.

It's all his fault. If he hadn't kissed Mydei—if he'd just kept it together, hadn't given in to that selfish desire of his that's always nagging at him for more—they wouldn't be here. Mydei wouldn't have looked at him like that, like he'd just broken something sacred between them by his words alone.

They should've been on their way back home by now, full of soda and popcorn, half-arguing over the film. Mydei would've been denying crying at the ending—again—and Phainon would've been teasing him over it. Maybe they'd stop for food on the way, maybe laugh about the silly parts of the film like the terrible CGI lions they brought out during a pit fight. That's how the night should've gone.

Instead, there's this. The quiet. The echo of raised voices still in his ears, the ghost of what they'd said—what he'd said—clinging to him like smoke. The silence feels like a punishment, and the emptiness of being alone again gnaws at him in ways he can't stand to name. Phainon rubs his face with both hands, but it doesn't help. The loneliness doesn't fade. It never truly does, it's only masked when he's with other people, but Mydei—his Mydei, his dearest Mydei—is the only one where it truly goes away. However, this time, the feeling just settles deeper, like a shadow that knows its way around his ribs too well, invasive and heavy.

"Here you go!" Castorice chirps, interrupting his thoughts as she dumps two towels into Phainon's arms. "Take as long as you need, okay? I'll be in the kitchen, and I'll make us a cup of tea. How does that sound?"

Phainon nods numbly, forcing a shaky smile on his face as Castorice's own brightens at it. He rifles through his duffel bag and pulls out a worn t-shirt and joggers and hands it over to her.

"I'll sort this out," Castorice says, patting him on the shoulder before she leaves, closing the door behind her.

Phainon sighs, his shoulders sagging under the weight of the cold and wet clothing he's in, and the pressure of being alone again. Before getting undressed, he turns the shower on in hopes it'll warm up quickly. The spray comes out hot and strong almost immediately, which he's grateful for.

He shrugs out of his jacket, pulling his sodden cashmere jumper over his head and listening to them splat on the floor as he drops them. He can't bring himself to care anymore, only focusing on one thing at a time. Phainon unbuttons the fly of his jeans and shimmies out of them, cringing as the thick material clings to his legs. He fishes his phone and keys out of his pocket and puts them on the side counter, not bothering to check for any messages. He doubts that Mydei's messaged him. Next, his socks, then last of all, his boxers, until he's standing there naked and shivering.

It doesn't take long for him to warm up under the hot spray, and as he scrubs himself down and washes his hair with Castorice's floral shampoo, he's reminded of the citrus scented stuff that Mydei uses instead. He sniffs sadly, eyes drooping and lips curling down as he washes the suds out of his hair.

Stupid, stupid Mydei and his stupid sweet citrus shower routine. Stupid, stupid Phainon for thinking about it when he's supposed to be trying to move on. Well, that's what he assumes he's supposed to be doing right now, at least. He can't stay in the past, dwelling on his unrequited feelings no matter how much he wants to roll around in self pity for a while. He imagines that as he washes off the bubbles, every piece of him connected to Mydei is going down the drain, spiralling and spinning out of control then disappearing.

It doesn't work, but it lifts his shoulders a little as the metaphorical weight of everything begins to shift. It's not all his fault, is it? Mydei was there as well, confusing him and making half-hearted comments that made no sense. Does he truly not feel anything for Phainon, was it all his wishful thinking the entire time? Or is what Mydei was saying—or at least, trying to say— was that he did have feelings, but just didn't want to be his boyfriend?

Phainon grumbles, scrubbing his nails into his scalp in the hopes that'll help iron things out. It doesn't, all it does it make his skin throb and sore. He sighs again, the sound getting lost in the steam, and decides it's time to get out.

He finds Castorice exactly where she said she'd be, in the kitchen, sitting at the dining table and sipping away at her cup of tea. She perks up when she sees him, her eyes sleepy and mouth pulled into a small smile as she greets him.

"Hey, Cas," Phainon replies, only clad in a towel wrapped high around his waist. He's fully dry, except for his hair which is still slightly damp. "Are my pyjamas all warmed up now?"

"They should be," Castorice replies, getting up and walking over to the radiator in the adjoining living room. She pats over them delicately, smiling, and then hands them over to Phainon. He takes them gratefully, giving her a quiet 'thank you' in response before going back into the bathroom to get changed.

He emerges again, fully clothed and nice and warm, hair mostly dry as he ruffled it again with one of the towels he was given. He doesn't care if it's sticking up in odd angles, it's not like Castorice is going to care, and it's not like Mydei is here to impress, either.

"Here, your tea. It should be cool enough now to drink," Castorice says, handing him over a small mug with flowers all over it. It's cute.

He takes a sip, eyelashes fluttering as the hot liquid runs down his throat, warming him up from the inside out. It's such a relief, and he takes a seat next to Castorice at the dining table. They sit in silence for a bit, but it's not a bad silence. It's clear that she's waiting for him to be ready to talk, but he's still not sure if he is. What would he even say? That they got into a fight over something that could've been avoided?

Phainon sighs, rubbing at his eyes with his fists as exhaustion sets in. "Is it okay if I stay here for a bit?" He asks.

"Of course it is!" Castorice replies. "Stay as long as you need, okay? I don't have a spare room, but my sofa is plenty big enough for your giant frame." She chuckles.

"I'm not that big!" Phainon opens his mouth to say more, to say that Mydei is bigger than he is, but he stops. Instead, he says: "Thanks, Cas. I really appreciate it." And for the first time, a real smile appears on his face.

She waves him off, taking a sip of her tea. "Do you want to talk about it?"

Phainon doesn't answer straight away. He hums, looking down at his drink and swirls it around a few times in the mug just to watch it move. Then he sighs and nods, shoulders slumping forward. "I confessed my feelings to Mydei—"

Castorice squeals, but then at Phainon's withering look, she mimics zipping up her lips and throwing away the key.

He huffs, the corner of his mouth twitching for half a second before he loses it again. "I confessed. It didn't go well. He didn't say he didn't love me back, but he also didn't say he did, either." His voice wavers, quieting on the last word. "He just said he wanted some space. Because apparently, I'm 'confused'." He lifts his fingers for the air quotes, shaking his head in dismay at repeating it all.

It all feels distant now—like it happened to someone else. The memory is blurred around the edges, smudged like ink dragged across wet paper. He remembers flashes, the sound of his own voice cracking mid-sentence, the way Mydei's expression had gone tight and unreadable, along with the space that'd never been there between them opening up and refusing to close again.

"I thought maybe if I said it…" Phainon begins. "If I got it all out there, it would stop eating at me. That I could fix things. But now it's worse, and I— I keep thinking about what he didn't say. How he just stood there and let me leave." He takes a shaky sip of his drink, the hot liquid now going down his throat like sludge. "I took him out to see City of Warriors, and I wanted it so badly to be a date. I told him that and he just said that we weren't dating and then he looked all confused and—"

"Breathe," Castorice reminds him, and he stops to take a gulping breath of air. "So you took him on a date, then what happened?"

"We… um…" He flushes bright red. "We kissed in the cinema…"

"Mhm," Castorice hums, but she looks like she's about to vibrate out of her skin.

Phainon sets his mug down and covers his face with his hands, feeling how warm his cheeks are. Even now, even after everything, the memory of kissing Mydei, feeling him whine and moan against his lips, still does something funny to his heart. "Gods, I'm so stupid."

"No, you're not," Castorice says. "You're human, and you love him. That's not being stupid."

"Feels like it," Phainon sighs, dropping his hands back onto the table. "I don't know what I'm supposed to do. Do I just move on? Can we go back to the way things used to be? I don't— I don't think I can pretend not to be in love with him anymore, Cas."

A sniffle comes from his right, and he whips his head around in shock to witness Castorice beginning to cry. "I'm sorry," She says, wiping her tears before they can fall fully. "I just… I adore you both so much, and it hurts that you're both hurting. I wish I could fix this for you, but I don't know what to do either."

"Cas…" Phainon trails off, reaching over to grab her hand. He squeezes it affectionately, "I'm sure it'll be okay. It's me and Mydei, right? We always sort things out." He says, but he doesn't believe himself. "I guess we really did need space from each other. I know I won't change my mind about how I feel about him, but maybe he will. Then we go from there."

Castorice nods, giving him a watery laugh in return. "Mydeimos loves you, too. He just has a funny way of showing it right now. It's so obvious that he's always felt the same way, we all noticed immediately. So don't give up hope, okay?!"

"Okay!" Phainon replies, smiling the best he can. Her pep talks always seem to help, even if he still feels a little unsure around the edges. "I don't know how long I'll be here for, but I'll try and not make myself a nuisance."

"Don't be silly," Castorice says. "You're never a nuisance. You're welcome to stay for as long as your back will allow you to sleep on my sofa."

"Hah! I'll be fine, no need to worry about that," Phainon replies. He stands up, downing the rest of his lukewarm tea. He wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. "I think it's time for bed."

"I'm so glad you said that," Castorice says, chuckling lightly as she places their empty mugs into the sink. Before he can say about washing them up for her, she says: "I'll do them later. I'll go sort out your pillows and quilt for the night."

As she does that, Phainon fishes his phone out of his pocket. He stares at the blank screen for a bit before gaining the courage to tap on it, waking it up. He blinks in shock as there's a litany of notifications waiting for him.

Mydei

Missed Call [35]

Mydei

Text messages [4]

"What the hell…" Phainon gasps, swiping away the missed call notifications in favour of clicking on the texts.

Mydei [11:45 pm]

Phainon.

Please come home.

I'm sorry.

I don't want space from you.

Phainon swallows down the lump in his throat. His hands tremble as he stares at the screen, the soft blue light painting his face in a glow that feels far too gentle for how violently his heart is pounding. The words blur for a second before he blinks them back into focus.

Please come home.

Home. The word hits him harder than he expects. For a moment, he can't breathe again, his heart beating wildly in his chest while not bringing in enough oxygen to compensate. Phainon reads the messages again and again —each one cutting through the fog that's been smothering him since he left. I'm sorry. I don't want space from you. The words he'd stopped letting himself hope for. And now they're here, sitting on his phone, fragile and impossible, waiting for him to believe them.

"Phainon?" Castorice's voice breaks through the silence. She's watching him carefully, a pillow and duvet gathered in her arms. She looks absolutely tiny in comparison to it, and Phainon wants to laugh but can't bring himself to when he looks back down again at his phone. "What is it?"

All he can do is turn the phone toward her, staring down at the floor as he does so.

Her expression softens immediately. "Oh dear," She whispers.

"Yeah," Phainon says, voice small and uneven. "He… he wants me to come home."

Castorice hesitates, clutching at the bedding a little tighter. "Do you want to?"

Phainon stares at the messages again, thoughts and heart still racing. Does he want to go home? Of course he does, but his pulse is so loud in his ears he can barely think straight. Part of him wants to run straight out the door, to go back, to see Mydei's face and believe that maybe this time it'll be okay. But another part—the bruised, trembling, louder part of him— remembers all too well how it felt to be pushed away. How it felt to be alone.

"I don't know," He answers honestly. "I don't know if I can handle whatever he has to say right now."

Castorice places the bedding down on the sofa and reaches over, resting a hand on his arm. "Then take a second. You don't need to decide right now."

Phainon nods, but his eyes stay locked on the messages, the glow of the screen reflecting in the sheen of unshed tears. He places his thumbs on the screen, ready to type, but he's not sure what he could say. What he should say. Does Mydei even deserve a reply right now? Should he leave it for when he's not feeling so emotional? He's already said enough—probably too much—and he doesn't want to make the same mistake again if he can help it.

He sighs, blowing a piece of hair out of his eye afterwards. He'll leave it for tonight, he won't say anything, and—

His phone vibrates in his hand.

Mydei [01:24 am]

Goodnight.

Phainon bites down on his bottom lip so hard he fears he's torn the skin, but thankfully there's no blooming taste of iron in his mouth. Just the sad feeling, the sad beat of his heart and the thickness in his throat he can't get rid of as he rereads the message.

With shaky fingers, he types:

Phainon [01:25 am]

Night.

Because he can't help himself. He can't not say anything, after all, not when Mydei is offering himself up like this. It's still too little too late, but maybe it's not as over as he once thought it was. Maybe they can fix this and get back to normal. But right now, he just wants to sleep.

"Thanks for getting me everything," Phainon says, putting his phone on do not disturb as he places it face down on the coffee table.

"No worries at all," Castorice replies, placing the pillow at one end of the sofa and fluffing it up before she flattens out the duvet over the top of the cushions. "I really hope you'll be okay sleeping there tonight…"

"I will, don't worry. Get some rest, I'm sorry for keeping you up so late."

"Good thing it's a Sunday now, hm?" Castorice replies, smiling at him. She pats him on the back and waves at him, "Goodnight, Phainon. Sleep well."

He nods in reply, "Sleep well, too."

His vision is dark, darker than black. It swallows him up whole, leeching into his skin and pores and into his organs, choking him. He's terrified, not knowing which way is up or down, not knowing how to get out of here. He tries to move his leg, but there's something wrapped around it, yanking it back into position without any give.

"Help—" He says, but it comes out garbled and wrong, like his voice is coming from behind him rather than in front. "Someone help me!"

Again, again and again he tries to move, but to no avail. To no avail his voice carries, getting stuck within the mass he finds himself in. He struggles, tugging and pulling, screaming and shouting until his throat is hoarse, all until finally there's a light ripping through the dark abyss, lighting up his way.

"Phainon," A voice says. It sounds like Mydei. All rough and deep and haggard around the edges, but still his Mydei. "Phainon." It says again, and he reaches out, desperately clawing his way out the remnants of darkness until he's fully in the light again, panting and soaked with sweat.

He looks up and finds Mydei standing there, but it's not his Mydei. It's someone else's, that he knows for sure. He looks like he's just stepped out of City of Warriors, all clad in red and bronze armour, golden boots and gauntlets that shine in the sudden sunlight that's beaming down on them. He squints against it, and that's when he realises he's on the floor, sprawled out and looking up in wonder at this Mydei before him.

"You have to go," This Mydei says to him, voice firm as he crosses his arms over his chest, glaring down at him. There's not an ounce of familiarity in his eyes, no warmth and no kindness. No nothing, and this solidifies the fact that this isn't his Mydei at all.

Even when his Mydei was mad at him, he still held something in those amber eyes for him. Something tangible, something he could latch onto and burrow away deep with.

"I don't want you anymore. You have to go."

"Mydei?" He questions, trying to move again to at least stand up so he's on the same level as this Mydei. It doesn't work, and he's left wriggling around on the floor, pinned down by something invisible. "Mydei?!" He says again, this time more panic in his voice.

"You have to go," Mydei repeats, and then everything becomes blurry, distorted and horrifying.

The scene melts away like wax, slurring and shimmering. Nothing makes sense, not as Mydei disappears into a blur and he himself becomes nothing more than a speck in the atmosphere. It's him that's causing it to burn, the heat coming off his limbs as wavering flames explode in front of him. It's him, it's him, it's…

"Mydei—"

His throat is full of ash.

"Mydei?"

His head hurts.

"Mydei!" Phainon yells, shooting up from the sofa, heart pounding like a drum. "Fuck…" He drops his head between his shoulders, shuddering as the waves of his nightmare come over him like the tide, ebbing and flowing until he stops shaking.

Phainon's covered in sweat, his fringe plastered to his forehead just like it was last night from the rain. He feels disgusting, clammy and cold all over. He grabs his phone from the coffee table, blinking at the time saying it's already gone well past 10 am. Castorice should be awake, but where is she?

He stands up, making sure to fold the quilt over neatly. He's still not sure how long he's going to be here. Phainon wanders into the kitchen, blinking in shock as he's suddenly hit with the smell of breakfast cooking: bacon, sausages, and eggs all fry away as the toaster pings up with toast.

"Cas?"

"Oh!" Castorice exclaims, jumping in fright as she turns to face him. She's fully dressed now, out of her nightgown and in a frilly shirt tucked into a skirt. "You're awake! I thought I heard you moving around."

"You didn't hear me yelling?" He asks in confusion.

"Yell—? No… did you have a nightmare?" Castorice asks, face creasing in worry.

"No, it's nothing. Don't worry," Phainon waves her off, taking a seat at the dining table.

She looks at him sceptically but doesn't push, of which he's very grateful.

"I bought you a toothbrush while you were sleeping," Castorice says as she plates up their food, graciously placing it right in front of Phainon. It smells delicious, and he digs in straight away, his stomach gurgling.

"Oh, thanks!" He forgot a lot back at home. He tries not to think about it, the raw sting of home, where Mydei currently is, as it still hurts.

But he can't help but wonder if Mydei is eating alone right now. They usually have breakfast around this time on Sundays—just something small, as they're both too tired to cook too much after a week of classes. Toast, maybe eggs if Mydei is feeling up for it, and a cup of coffee so strong that it wakes them both straight up. Phainon can picture it so clearly that it aches: the soft rumble of the kettle boiling, the smell of toast, the faint sound of Mydei humming under his breath as he drifts through the kitchen, his strong back on show as Phainon watches from the dining table.

Phainon places a hand over his chest, as if it can soothe the sting there.

Maybe Mydei's sitting at the table right now, stirring his tea or coffee for too long because he's lost in thought. Maybe he's not eating at all. Maybe he's sad that Phainon isn't there, or maybe he's relieved. Maybe he's still in bed, sprawled across the sheets, hair messy and face pressed into the pillow.

That thought makes his throat tighten and his cheeks warm. The last time he'd been in Mydei's bed was when he last had a nightmare, and then they'd… Well. He doesn't want to dwell on it, not when Castorice is right next to him digging into her breakfast. He clears his throat and tries to think of something else, but his thoughts bring him straight back to Mydei.

It's strange—how quickly a home can feel hollow depending on the people inside of it. How routines built out of love and comfort can collapse overnight, leaving nothing but ghosts behind. The kitchen table, their matching mugs, even the damn fancy cereal that Mydei always buys him despite him saying not to—they all feel heavier in Phainon's mind now that he isn't there to share them.

He wonders if Mydei misses him. If he's glancing towards the empty chair without meaning to. Whether he's up thinking about how quiet the flat must be without Phainon's chatter filling it up. It's not like he doesn't want to go home, he aches for it, especially if it means that he can see Mydei like he was before everything went wrong. He just wants to pretend for a while that it's all okay, that Mydei is here next to him.

But instead, he's here—staring down at his breakfast, suddenly not very hungry anymore, and even as he takes a swig of tea that Castorice prepared for him, it doesn't taste right. It doesn't taste like their tea bags at home, doesn't taste like their water. Phainon pictures Mydei doing the same thing across the city, wondering if they're both just… lost, orbiting around each other from a distance that neither of them know how to close.

"Do you not like it?" Castorice asks, her voice sounding small.

Phainon snaps out of it, turning to face his friend. "I was thinking of Mydei." He answers honestly.

She nods like she gets it, and perhaps she does. "You don't need to eat if you don't want to. But it might make you feel worse if you don't."

He nods, and takes a mouthful of toast with bacon on top. It does taste good, not ashen like in his dreams, but not as good as the smoked rich variety that Mydei cooks for him. However, none of that matters. What does matter is that he's still being taken care of wherever he is, even if it’s not with Mydei.

"I'll do the dishes," Phainon offers, not wanting to be a total leech while he's staying here. He's already intruded enough, and knowing he's going to stay here for longer makes him feel even worse.

"That's okay, we can do them together!" Castorice replies.

"Sure!" Phainon says, grinning at her.

They finish their breakfast in silence, the only sounds of them chewing and cutlery clicking against the plates. It's peaceful, and it helps settle the restlessness inside of him, even just a tiny bit.

With the dishes washed and stacked away, they collapse onto the sofa. The soft buzz from the TV fills the silence, muted to a little more than a whisper. Castorice shifts to face him, one knee tucked beneath her, eyes bright with concern and resolve.

"Alright," She says gently. "We need an action plan!"

"Can I at least brush my teeth first?" Phainon jokes, laughing when he gets a playful shove in response.

"Sure, go brush them. But when you're back, we're getting serious."

Phainon grabs the toothbrush Castorice got for him and rushes to the bathroom. He doesn't want to look at himself in the mirror as he goes through the motions of brushing his teeth, but it's hard not to when there's a giant one right opposite him. He glances up and catches his own reflection, squinting at it like he's staring at a stranger.

His hair is a mess—flattened in place, wild in others—and his eyes are red-rimmed and puffy. There's a faint salt stain on his cheek from where he assumes he was crying during his sleep. He feels a bubble of shame and embarrassment come up, knowing that Castorice had seen it and hadn't mentioned anything. All in all, he looks exhausted in every sense of the word. Hollow. Like someone who hasn't slept very well. Which, he realises, after his nightmare, might be true.

He swishes the toothpaste around his mouth and leans over the sink, trying to ignore the lump forming in his throat. So many times he and Mydei had brushed their teeth side by side, elbows knocking and grins stretched across their faces as they try to finish brushing their teeth before the other. They'd always end up either in a draw, or even odds, so it never really mattered in the end. Even though Mydei has his own bathroom, he'd still join him to brush his teeth and wash his face on the occasion. Right now, that's all Phainon can think of, and it almost sets him off crying again as he spits out the remnants of toothpaste lingering in his mouth.

He grabs a wad of toilet paper and wipes his mouth, throwing it in the bin afterwards. He goes back to staring at his reflection for a little bit. The man in the mirror doesn't look like someone who used to wake up to laughter and warmth, but instead one who dearly misses it.

And gods, does he already miss it. Phainon misses Mydei.

He's not sure how long it'll take for him to fully adapt to his new reality—or if he ever will.

It turns out, he can only go just under a week before Castorice breaks.

He's spent the past few days in a fugue state. The sofa has become his entire world—his bed, his refuge, his prison. He barely moves except to eat or stumble to the bathroom, the cushions practically moulding to the shape of his body. His back is starting to ache now, just like how Castorice warned him it would if he continued sleeping there, but whenever he thinks of leaving and going home he starts to feel like he's going to throw up. Maybe he's left it too long now and he'll never be able to go back, doomed to stay on Castorice's couch and take up space. It's supposed to feel safe here, this little corner of stillness, but it isn't. Not really.

Not when the nightmares are so bad. They come every time he closes his eyes. They're relentless, clawing through the edges of his sleep until he wakes up gasping. They're worse now—worse than they've been since his parents and sister passed away in a house fire. Back then, the dreams were about loss; now, they're about him. About Mydei.

Except it's never his Mydei in these dreams. It's someone else's—always someone else's—and they all look at him the same way: with pity, with distance, with the certainty that he'll never matter the way he wants to. That he'll never be enough. He wakes drenched in sweat each time, shivering and breathless, clutching at his quilt like it's the only thing keeping him tethered to this world. Most of his clothes are damp from it now, dark patches sprouting around the neck hem and underneath his arms. Even sometimes on his lower back. It's proof of how far he's slipped, he supposes. Castorice never mentions it when she collects them for washing—she just gives him that soft, careful look that makes his stomach twist.

She never says she's worried. She doesn't have to. He can feel it in the way she lingers by the sofa a little longer each day, as if she's afraid he might fade away entirely if she looks the other way.

It all comes to a head on Friday, six days after he fled.

"I let you off earlier this week, but now I'm serious. We need an action plan. You're moping," Castorice says, hands on her hips as she stands in front of Phainon who's sitting on the sofa, trying to watch TV. "You haven't shaved in a week, barely eaten, haven't slept, and you're constantly checking your phone. He isn't going to text you if you don't reply!"

Phainon sniffs and nods, "I know…"

Castorice sighs, letting her hands drop down to her sides. "Don't make me the villain, Phainon. I'm just trying to help."

He sits up straight at that, distraught at the thought of Castorice feeling like that. "I know you are! And I can't thank you enough for taking care of me —"

"I've been so busy with coursework I've barely seen you for the past week," She says gently, coming to sit next to him on the sofa. "And I'm sorry about that. Mydei's been asking after you at uni, did you know? He—"

"Really?" Phainon asks too quickly.

"Yes," She stresses, patting him on the head. "So, I have an idea."

"Oh yeah?" Phainon asks. "Time to kick me out?"

"Absolutely not," Castorice guffaws. "I have a friend on my course who's holding a house party tomorrow. You're invited."

"Huh?" Phainon says, "But I don't know them."

Castorice rolls her eyes, "That's the fun about house parties. It's only going to be a small gathering, but I explained that you're staying with me and she said you can come. It'll get you out of the house, and maybe you can have some fun."

"I'm not sure I'm in the mood…"

"Then get in the mood. You're coming, alright? I won't take no for an answer! I need someone to come with me and hide away in the corner, okay?" She says conspiratorially, giggling at the end. "I'm bringing a book with me, and we're all pretty chill on my course. So don't worry too much."

Phainon slowly begins to nod his head, the idea washing over him in pieces until he's made up his mind. "Okay," He says. "I'll come."

Castorice claps and cheers, leaning over to give him a quick hug. "I'm so glad! Alright, okay, you still have those nice clothes you came in before, so you can wear them again. I've already washed and folded them, so they're ready to go."

Phainon grimaces at the thought of wearing the clothes that Mydei picked out for him. But everything else he bought was… Well, not wearable to a party. He'd been living in cringey graphic tees and loose joggers for the past week. Even his boxers weren't safe, most of them being of the brightly coloured variety that Mydei always used to scoff at and make fun of whenever he folded them for him. Phainon harrumphs to himself at that thought, crossing his arms over his chest as he sulks at the idea of being made fun of by Mydei.

Stupid, stupid Mydei.

And yet stupid, stupid Phainon for still being hung up on him.

He thought that, given enough time, his feelings would dull at least a little —that they'd fade into something softer, something easier to carry. But they haven't. If anything, they've only grown wilder, more unruly, sprawling through his chest like an untamed vine. He can't get over Mydei, and he doesn't think he ever will. He doesn't want to get over Mydei. He loves loving him, adores him, even, and it's made him into the person he is today; no matter how depressed that said person is right now.

Every attempt to suppress his feelings just makes it worse. The ache resurfaces in new ways—at the sound of a laugh that almost sounds like his, at the sight of an empty mug on the counter, at the ghost of Mydei's washing detergent that still lingers on his clothes.
